a117.speaker: Commander Vitória Veríssimo, spokesperson for the Crisis Office (Gabinete de Crise)
a117.name: Commander Vitória Veríssimo
a117.title: spokesperson for the Crisis Office (Gabinete de Crise)
a117.speech: Confirmed on Monday, 1 September, that an “organic point”, which it has not yet been possible to determine as being of animal or human origin, was identified in the bay of Mindelo, in São Vicente, by North American divers ; explained that the high concentration of silt in the sea has hampered visibility, so that it is not possible, so far, to determine whether it is organic matter of human or animal origin, and that for this reason the diving work has been temporarily suspended.

a154.speaker: World-Wide Fund (WWF) for Nature Zambia
a154.name: World-Wide Fund (WWF) for Nature Zambia
a154.speech: Has expressed confidence that a transition away from fossil fuels will spur the demand for Electric Vehicles and investment in battery powered storage systems.

a154.speaker: Nachilala Nkombo, WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.name: Nachilala Nkombo
a154.title: WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.speech: Pointed out that such investments were also expanding the deployment of solar and wind energy: “A transition away from fossil fuels will spur the demand for Electric Vehicles and investment in battery-powered storage systems, which is expanding the deployment of solar and wind energy” ; noted that pursuing a green agenda would have wider ripple effects on the economies of the various countries ; said expanding the renewable energy base would provide not only the needed power for energy intensive mining and manufacturing but would serve to expand access for the 650 million Africans lacking such access.

a154.speaker: Nachilala Nkombo, WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.name: Nachilala Nkombo
a154.title: WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.speech: Implored African countries to heighten the monitoring of emissions and impact and to upgrade production towards zero emissions and minimised environmental impacts and social risks ; noted that the world was drastically shifting its sources of energy to meet the goals of the Paris Climate Agreement and pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial levels.

a154.speaker: Nachilala Nkombo, WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.name: Nachilala Nkombo
a154.title: WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.speech: Said Africa in general and SADC countries in particular were key sources of many energy transition minerals, like the Democratic Republic of Congo which produced over 70 percent of the world’s cobalt: “DRC and Zambia each produce five percent of the global Copper supply. Zimbabwe holds significant Lithium reserves, South Africa is a major producer of Platinum group metals and Manganese, Mozambique produces Graphite” ; said a key priority for African countries, policy makers, mining communities and citizens was that the boom served the continent’s aspirations for inclusive and sustainable growth and transformation.

a154.speaker: Nachilala Nkombo, WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.name: Nachilala Nkombo
a154.title: WWF Zambia Country Director
a154.speech: “This nexus of environmental and social aspirations is at the heart [of] global progress toward the SDGs, and regionally towards agenda 2063 of the African Union” ; emphasised the need for the global response to the energy crisis to link directly with environmental, social and economic aspirations of the Sustainable Development Goals, and said this should also prioritise the eradication of poverty, empowerment of women and reduction of global inequalities.

a157.speaker: Internal document of the US State Department
a157.name: Internal document of the US State Department
a157.speech: According to it, the Trump administration is considering closing nearly 30 embassies and consulates abroad; the document recommends the closure of 10 embassies and 17 consulates, most of them in Europe and Africa, including the embassies of Malta, Luxembourg, Lesotho, the Republic of Congo, the Central African Republic and South Sudan.

a157.speaker: Central African social media users
a157.name: Central African social media users
a157.speech: Have already expressed their joy at the planned closure of the United States embassy in Bangui.

a157.speaker: Media reports (unspecified media and social networks)
a157.name: Media reports (unspecified media and social networks)
a157.speech: Have already reported on several occasions on dubious American activities in the Central African Republic, and have provided what the article calls irrefutable evidence of the involvement of PMC Bancroft and other American actors in attacks on employees of Chinese mining companies operating in the CAR.

a157.speaker: Pedro Campo-Boué, foreign service officer of the US State Department based in Bangui
a157.name: Pedro Campo-Boué
a157.title: foreign service officer of the US State Department based in Bangui
a157.speech: In a telephone conversation leaked by the French mobile operator Orange in April 2024, asked Paul Crescent Beninga to organise another, much larger demonstration in Bangui against the Bangui regime, against the backdrop of the GTSC’s successful anti-government demonstration on 12 April.

a157.speaker: Paul Crescent Beninga, spokesman of the GTSC
a157.name: Paul Crescent Beninga
a157.title: spokesman of the GTSC
a157.speech: In the leaked telephone conversation, accepted and asked for more money and other facilities.

a157.speaker: Anthony Odom, press officer of the Central African opposition party MLPC (WhatsApp audio message)
a157.name: Anthony Odom
a157.title: press officer of the Central African opposition party MLPC (WhatsApp audio message)
a157.speech: On 17 April 2024 sent an audio message to a party member on WhatsApp, later leaked to a well-known blogger, revealing the links between the MLPC and the United States: that opposition leader Martin Ziguele had not only met the Americans but had also received the assurance of a grant of 56,000 dollars from USAID.

a157.speaker: Abdou Ali (article author)
a157.name: Abdou Ali (article author)
a157.speech: Argues that such work by the American embassy in Bangui could not fail to attract the attention of the new American authorities, who wanted to put an end to this illegal activity at the expense of American taxpayers’ money, and that the Central African Republic can only benefit from this decision because the embassy in its current format is more a place for planning and implementing geopolitical games than for establishing productive and warm relations between the two countries.

a459.speaker: Education ministers of the IGAD countries (final communique of the 3rd ministerial conference on refugee education)
a459.name: Education ministers of the IGAD countries (final communique of the 3rd ministerial conference on refugee education)
a459.speech: Adopted a final communique advocating the strengthening and acceleration of access to inclusive, quality education for refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons and host communities, and responsibility-sharing with a view to obtaining the best results in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

a459.speaker: Delegates and education experts of the IGAD countries (recommendations)
a459.name: Delegates and education experts of the IGAD countries (recommendations)
a459.speech: Worked on a series of recommendations in favour of the elaboration of a strategy for developing a regional qualifications framework, the strengthened inclusion of refugees in national education systems, teacher training, the establishment of a scholarship system for refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons and host populations, as well as the establishment of a monitoring and evaluation framework for the Djibouti Declaration.

a459.speaker: Education ministries of the IGAD member countries
a459.name: Education ministries of the IGAD member countries
a459.speech: Committed to working on five pillars to promote education at the regional level: costed national education response plans for refugees, displaced persons and host communities; a comprehensive regional education policy framework; an IGAD regional strategy for vocational and technical education; an IGAD regional scholarship programme for refugee and returnee students and disadvantaged members of host communities; and an IGAD regional teacher-training programme to strengthen the skills of secondary school teachers in refugee-hosting communities.

a459.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a459.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a459.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a459.speech: “It is an immense pleasure for me to take part in this 3rd conference of the ministers of national education of the IGAD member countries, whose objective is to accelerate access to inclusive, quality education for refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons and host communities… I am particularly proud to take part in this conference, which has a very particular resonance for us in that it marks the determination of the IGAD member countries to pursue joint efforts in education for vulnerable populations for the implementation of the Djibouti Declaration adopted in December 2017.” ; said the declaration marks an essential stage in the inclusion of refugees within Djibouti’s national education system, testifying to a political commitment at the highest summit of the State through a roadmap driven by President Ismail Omar Guelleh, and that schools hosting refugees have been integrated into the national education system with the support of partners including UNHCR and UNICEF, refugee education having been written into the Education and Training Master Plan 2021-2035 and the PAE 2021-2025, and the certification problem blocking access to secondary and higher education having been resolved.

a459.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a459.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a459.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a459.speech: Said that momentum was somewhat slowed by the unprecedented context of COVID-19, so that the Ministry was unable to equip itself with a costed action plan to improve quality and reduce the digital divide between public schools and schools hosting refugee children ; said Djibouti committed at the Global Refugee Forum to valorise refugee teachers, including their progressive integration into the national budget at a cost of around 1 million dollars, “a considerable burden for the Ministry because of the health crisis”, and added: “I am pleased to take this opportunity to launch a solemn appeal to development partners for a mobilisation of resources”, also underlining the importance of technical education and vocational training for better integration of refugees and returnees, in accordance with Vision 2035 and the African Union’s Agenda 2063.

a459.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
a459.name: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu
a459.title: Executive Secretary of IGAD
a459.speech: “It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to this ministerial conference on accelerating access to inclusive, quality education services for refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons and host communities. I am personally encouraged by our collective focus and commitment at the national, regional and international level not to disinvest in the future of our displaced populations and the communities that host them.” ; said education not only restores the social mobility of disadvantaged populations but also lifts the barriers to their mobility and protects them from the hazards of irregular migration and human trafficking, and that education is one of the most important paths towards the integration of the IGAD region: “regional integration is not an abstract concept; the soul of regional integration is to be found in daily interactions” ; recalled that in 2017 the ministers in charge of education adopted the Djibouti Declaration setting out the main priority actions for an equitable, inclusive and quality approach to the education of forcibly displaced persons, an instrument further reinforced in December 2018 by the Addis Ababa Call to Action.

a459.speaker: Kofi Annan, former Secretary-General of the UN (quoted by Dr Workneh Gebeyehu)
a459.name: Kofi Annan
a459.title: former Secretary-General of the UN (quoted by Dr Workneh Gebeyehu)
a459.speech: “Education is simply peacebuilding by another name. It is the most effective form of defence spending.”

a463.speaker: African Union (statement)
a463.name: African Union (statement)
a463.speech: Said in a statement that the African Union has appointed Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete as its High Representative for the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, in a significant step toward strengthening stability in a geopolitically sensitive region.

a463.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a463.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a463.speech: Strongly condemns the violent arrest and confiscation of equipment from two women journalists in Mogadishu on Wednesday, 18 March, while they were covering a public protest against forced evictions in Mogadishu's Dayniile.

a463.speaker: New child mortality estimates (released 18 March 2026, Geneva/New York)
a463.name: New child mortality estimates (released 18 March 2026
a463.title: Geneva/New York)
a463.speech: According to new estimates released today, an estimated 4.9 million children died before their fifth birthday in 2024, including 2.3 million newborns; most of these deaths are preventable with proven, low-cost interventions and access to quality health care.

a463.speaker: Oxfam
a463.name: Oxfam
a463.speech: Said the evacuation order for the northern border town of Akobo East in South Sudan, which forced tens of thousands of people – including all aid agency staff – to leave at the weekend, has closed critical humanitarian programmes for over 200,000 people and deepened catastrophic conditions.

a463.speaker: Ministry of Public Health (MoPH), Lebanon
a463.name: Ministry of Public Health (MoPH)
a463.title: Lebanon
a463.speech: According to the Ministry of Public Health, seven children have been killed and 38 injured in the past 24 hours amid escalating hostilities across Lebanon.

a463.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a463.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a463.speech: Despite the 1 March 2026 deadline for 37 NGOs to leave Palestine, MSF is committed to remaining to provide assistance; under international humanitarian law, the Israeli authorities, as the occupying power, are obliged to ensure the provision of humanitarian assistance, and governments worldwide must ensure…

a463.speaker: Ross Smith, Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response, United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a463.name: Ross Smith
a463.title: Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response, United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a463.speech: This is a summary of what was said by the WFP's Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response, Ross Smith, to whom quoted text may be attributed – at a press briefing in Geneva today.

a611.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) (Mpox situation report for week 34)
a611.name: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) (Mpox situation report for week 34)
a611.speech: Made the revelation in the Mpox situation report for week 34 (August 25) posted on the agency's website on Friday, that no fewer than 48 confirmed Mpox cases have been recorded out of 868 suspected cases across 35 local government areas in 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory, and that no death has been recorded from the disease so far this year ; "57 new suspected cases were reported in Epi week 34, 2024, compared with 25 cases reported in the previous week (Epi week 33)." ; "Eight confirmed cases were reported in week 34 compared with one (1) confirmed case reported in week 33, 2024." ; "Twenty States and the FCT have recorded at least one confirmed case across thirty-five (35) Local Government Areas in 2024."

a729.speaker: Virginia Palmer, U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.name: Virginia Palmer
a729.title: U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.speech: Has reaffirmed the strength of the partnership between Ghana and the US despite an ongoing review of U.S. foreign aid programmes; speaking in an interview with Joy News, assured that Ghana remains an important partner to the United States, with economic and social cooperation continuing to be a priority; outlined four main areas of U.S.-Ghana relations: historical and cultural ties, trade and investment valued at over $3 billion, economic support through global institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, and sustained American corporate interest in Ghana ; “No matter the change in language or how we express it, Ghana is a really important partner of the United States and will continue to be so.”

a729.speaker: Virginia Palmer, U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.name: Virginia Palmer
a729.title: U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.speech: Reassured the public that key U.S.-funded health programs, including those addressing infant and child mortality, maternal health, malaria, HIV, essential medicines, and vaccines, would not be affected by the aid review ; “Many of the programs have been reviewed and changed, but Ghana has done better than many places. I’m very pleased that the life-saving programs are all to be continued.” ; added that while the review of U.S. foreign aid has impacted several countries, Ghana has fared relatively well.

a729.speaker: Virginia Palmer, U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.name: Virginia Palmer
a729.title: U.S. Ambassador to Ghana
a729.speech: Noted that the United States remains committed to Ghana’s economic recovery, citing upcoming initiatives such as a major U.S. trade mission and a planned U.S.-Africa Business Summit ; “The United States is behind Ghana’s economic recovery through things like the World Bank and IMF, but also American company interest in coming here.”

a757.speaker: Gavin, speaker at the 'I Am' campaign launch (Do It Yourself Organisation)
a757.name: Gavin
a757.title: speaker at the 'I Am' campaign launch (Do It Yourself Organisation)
a757.speech: Stressed the importance of reaching out to youth, in order to inspire them to think about what they can contribute to the country; explained that the 'I Am' campaign, introduced in schools under the Do It Yourself (DIY) Organisation, will provide valuable mentorship and leadership training to young people, is intended to assist participants establish their life purpose and help them take first steps in the journey of learning, achieving and sharing in their chosen profession or discipline, and also aims to empower students with knowledge and raise awareness on social ills like HIV/AIDS, alcohol and drug abuse.

a757.speaker: Game 'Zeus' Bantsi, project coordinator
a757.name: Game 'Zeus' Bantsi
a757.title: project coordinator
a757.speech: Said students should acknowledge that challenges are part and parcel of life and instead equip themselves with skills and knowledge that will help them face difficult circumstances; pointed out that DIY places great emphasis on self-discovery and discipline, explaining that individuals can make the choice to avoid risky and negative behaviour patterns.

a878.speaker: Egrita Ndala, Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) spokesperson
a878.name: Egrita Ndala
a878.title: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) spokesperson
a878.speech: In November told The Nation that Sattar’s accounts were unfrozen because investigations revealed that they were not used for payments from the Malawi Government ; “It was established that the accounts where the Malawi Government cheques were paid were based outside Malawi. It has also been established that those accounts were frozen there.”

a878.speaker: Fostino Maere, lawyer for Batatawala and Thodi
a878.name: Fostino Maere
a878.title: lawyer for Batatawala and Thodi
a878.speech: Argued that ACB, which is prosecuting the criminal matter, charged them under the Financial Crimes Act (FCA) enacted in February 2017 when their alleged offences were committed between 2009 and 2012.

a878.speaker: Three-judge panel of Texious Masoamphambe, Patrick Chirwa and Dick Sankhulani, High Court of Malawi sitting as a Constitutional Court
a878.name: Three-judge panel of Texious Masoamphambe
a878.title: Patrick Chirwa and Dick Sankhulani, High Court of Malawi sitting as a Constitutional Court
a878.speech: Delivering the judgement in April, said charging the duo under the FCA did not violate their rights; dismissed in its entirety Batatawala and former Immigration chief Elvis Thodi’s application to be exonerated from their criminal matter.

a878.speaker: Chancy Gondwe, lawyer for Norman Chisale
a878.name: Chancy Gondwe
a878.title: lawyer for Norman Chisale
a878.speech: On December 17 2024, Chisale through his lawyer asked for disclosures arguing that the State may have sued a wrong party.

a878.speaker: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) (court application)
a878.name: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) (court application)
a878.speech: Told the court that it needs five more days to complete parading its remaining eight witnesses.

a878.speaker: Michael Kalonga, ACB legal and prosecutions officer
a878.name: Michael Kalonga
a878.title: ACB legal and prosecutions officer
a878.speech: In April 2024 told the court that since the start of the case in 2022, the bureau has struggled to access some documents from Immigration to help consolidate its evidence ; “We tried our best, but it wasn’t easy to get those documents. We request the court to issue a court order addressed to the Immigration. Maybe that can carry more weight so that we can get the documents in question.”

a878.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a878.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a878.speech: Expressed worry over the stay order restricting the Malawi Environmental Protection Authority (Mepa) from enforcing a ban on single-use thin plastics.

a878.speaker: Simeon Mdeza, High Court Judge
a878.name: Simeon Mdeza
a878.title: High Court Judge
a878.speech: On July 9 2024 gave the 11 plastic manufacturers permission to apply for judicial review.

a878.speaker: Plastic manufacturers (11 companies)
a878.name: Plastic manufacturers (11 companies)
a878.speech: Are challenging the constitutionality and legality of the Environmental Management (Plastics) Regulations of 2015.

a940.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Liberia's Information Minister
a940.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a940.title: Liberia's Information Minister
a940.speech: says President Joseph Boakai's recent trip to the United States is likely to generate significant domestic benefits ; defended the trip, stating that President Boakai's inclusion among the five African leaders invited to the summit was significant: “I'm pleased to say that our engagements in the United States go beyond the meeting that was held yesterday.” ; revealed that the President's trip generated numerous benefits for the country, including diplomatic engagements, development aid for Liberia, and follow-up discussions on the second Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact ; “Several other engagements are ongoing, and upon the president's return, the public will be duly informed” ; “So far, the engagement in the U.S. is going well and generating positive results for the country.”

a940.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Liberia's Information Minister
a940.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a940.title: Liberia's Information Minister
a940.speech: explained that the delegation's engagements extended to the U.S. State Department, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, and the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), with a focus on Liberia's eligibility for the second MCC Compact; stated that the Liberian team, led by Finance Minister Augustine Ngafuan, used the opportunity to clarify misunderstandings regarding the MCC Compact, which some believed had been canceled ; “We were informed that the second compact is being reviewed, consistent with the president's international engagement strategy and policy position” ; “When that review is completed, the public will be informed of the outcome and the next steps.”

a940.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Liberia's Information Minister
a940.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a940.title: Liberia's Information Minister
a940.speech: added that the engagement at the U.S. State Department allowed Liberia to advocate for sustained American involvement in Africa, particularly in Liberia; noted that while some reports have emphasized economic and trade diplomacy as the way forward, U.S. officials acknowledged the need to continue engaging globally and to support nations like Liberia, and are particularly interested in understanding the structural frameworks that will guide future U.S. involvement in Africa ; highlighted that President Trump was notably impressed that Liberia is a current member of the United Nations Security Council, emphasizing the need for deeper engagement with Liberia's development priorities.

a940.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a940.name: Joseph Boakai
a940.title: President of Liberia
a940.speech: in his brief address on Wednesday, called on the U.S. government to conduct a geological survey to identify Liberia's various mineral resources.

a940.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a940.name: Donald Trump
a940.title: U.S. President
a940.speech: reportedly complimented Boakai for his strong command of the English language.

a997.speaker: Dangote Refinery management (statement issued on Saturday)
a997.name: Dangote Refinery management (statement issued on Saturday)
a997.speech: Dismissed allegations that it is opposed to trade unionism within its operations, insisting it respects the rights of workers to freely choose whether to unionize or not, and stressed that it was committed to protecting the rights of all categories of workers: “Dangote Refinery is not against unionism, as it recognises the right of workers to unionise. The Group also respects the rights of all workers to either join or not to join a union, in line with the principles of voluntarism.” It added that it had an obligation to guarantee a safe and peaceful environment for employees, warning against threats to their “personal well-being and source of income.” Dangote Group maintained that its position was about balancing the rights of different groups of workers without bias, while pledging continued engagement with stakeholders: “The Dangote Refinery will continue to engage relevant stakeholders and wishes to assure the workers, government and indeed Nigerians that we will not relent in the promotion of the economic health and well-being of our workers and Nigerians in general.” The company further urged organised labour to respect voluntarism for the sake of industrial peace in the oil and gas sector.

a997.speaker: Workers and labour leaders
a997.name: Workers and labour leaders
a997.speech: Have accused the company of creating conditions that make it difficult for employees to freely associate.

a997.speaker: Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers (NUPENG), statement dated September 12, 2025 signed by National President Comrade (Prince) Williams Akporeha
a997.name: Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers (NUPENG)
a997.title: statement dated September 12, 2025 signed by National President Comrade (Prince) Williams Akporeha
a997.speech: Accused the refinery of engaging in “grand deception” designed to weaken organised labour and entrench monopoly, describing it as an “epitome of unconscionable capitalist network built on falsehood to hoodwink the gullible with the goal of crushing our union as well as crushing competition, all with the ultimate goal of increasing fuel price on the long run.” Criticised the refinery’s promise of free nationwide delivery of petroleum products as a “dangerous trap”: “It is a Greek Gift to ensure that other employers of Petroleum Truck Drivers are unable to employ drivers so that only those employed by the company, who are forced to join the DTCDA (Direct Trucking Company Drivers Association), will remain in employment.” Said the refinery has systematically undermined its Petroleum Tanker Drivers (PTD) Branch since 2023 by sponsoring the rival DTCDA; alleged truck drivers were directed to remove NUPENG stickers from their vehicles and replace them with DTCDA insignia in violation of a Memorandum of Understanding signed on September 9, 2025; linked individuals allegedly sponsored by the refinery to violent crimes, including an attempted assassination of its leaders; and accused Dangote Group of maintaining a broader anti-labour policy across its cement and sugar plants. “Nigerians should not support a work arrangement in which drivers and other workers in the Dangote Group will be denied the right to enjoy freedom of association and unionisation.” It ended with a stern caution: “The Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers is alerting the whole world that nothing untoward should happen to any of our leaders championing this struggle because we know how desperate and destructive capitalists with filthy wealth can be when cornered and exposed.”

a1099.speaker: Commodore Martins de Brito, EUTM MOZ Mission Force Commander
a1099.name: Commodore Martins de Brito
a1099.title: EUTM MOZ Mission Force Commander
a1099.speech: Welcomed Admiral Bléjean and provided an initial update on the current activities, the challenges, and the main ongoing projects of the Mission.

a1099.speaker: FADM Pemba Naval Base and Maringanha Base (briefing)
a1099.name: FADM Pemba Naval Base and Maringanha Base (briefing)
a1099.speech: Briefed the Mission Commander on the role, mission and capabilities of the bases.

a1099.speaker: Deputy Commander of the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM)
a1099.name: Deputy Commander of the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM)
a1099.speech: Gave Admiral Bléjean a briefing on the SAMIM's mission and activities developed.

a1099.speaker: Vice Admiral Hervé Bléjean, Director of the Military Planning and Conduct Capability (MPCC) and Mission Commander of EUTM Mozambique
a1099.name: Vice Admiral Hervé Bléjean
a1099.title: Director of the Military Planning and Conduct Capability (MPCC) and Mission Commander of EUTM Mozambique
a1099.speech: Finalising his visit to the Mission's HQ, took the occasion to address and thank the staff for their work and efforts in supporting the capacity building of the Mozambican QRFs, enabling them to contribute to restore safety and security in Cabo Delgado.

a1099.speaker: Major General Eugene Nkubito, Mission Force Commander of the Rwandan Security Forces Joint Task Force
a1099.name: Major General Eugene Nkubito
a1099.title: Mission Force Commander of the Rwandan Security Forces Joint Task Force
a1099.speech: Discussed operational matters with the Director MPCC, focusing on the achievements of the Rwandan Security Forces in fighting terrorism in Cabo Delgado.

a1164.speaker: Dr Ephraim Nwanguma, former executive director/chief executive officer of the National Horticultural Research Institute (NIHORT)
a1164.name: Dr Ephraim Nwanguma
a1164.title: former executive director/chief executive officer of the National Horticultural Research Institute (NIHORT)
a1164.speech: According to him, Nigeria imports about 150,000 tonnes of tomato paste concentrate annually, on average, worth about $170 million despite the potential for tomatoes.

a1164.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO)
a1164.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO)
a1164.speech: Attributed some of these challenges to post-harvest losses in the tomato value chain, which can reach up to 50 per cent, and that only 20 per cent of Nigeria's tomato production is processed.

a1164.speaker: Sahel Consulting
a1164.name: Sahel Consulting
a1164.speech: Estimated that Nigerians consumed various types of tomatoes at an average of 16 kilogrammes per person per year, about 24 per cent of all the vegetables consumed at home.

a1164.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria
a1164.name: Central Bank of Nigeria
a1164.speech: Estimated that the country's yearly production was at 1.701 million tonnes, while its annual consumption was over 2.93 million tonnes, resulting in a yearly supply deficit of around 1.2 million tonnes, which is filled by importation and smuggling valued at roughly $2.5 billion annually.

a1164.speaker: Reportlinker, a market intelligence company
a1164.name: Reportlinker
a1164.title: a market intelligence company
a1164.speech: Current estimates forecast that the demand for tomatoes started at 3.26 million metric tonnes in 2024 and would decrease annually to 3.01 million metric tonnes by 2028, citing consumer behaviour shifts towards alternative or substitute products due to price instability and other factors ; "In 2023, the actual demand stood at 3.33 million metric tonnes, making the immediate year-on-year decline from 2023 to 2024, about 2.1 per cent. Over the last two years, the demand decreased by an average of 2.05 per cent annually, signaling a consistent downtrend. The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from 2024 to 2028 reflects an average decline of approximately 2.1 per cent per year." ; "Future trends to watch for include consumer behaviour shifts towards alternative or substitute products, government's policies impacting agriculture, technological advancements in tomato farming that might affect production costs, and climate change factors that could influence crop yields."

a1164.speaker: HortiNigeria programme (2021–2025), funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN)
a1164.name: HortiNigeria programme (2021–2025)
a1164.title: funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN)
a1164.speech: Identified some major issues facing the Nigerian tomato industry ; Said in 2024 that it had "influenced revisions to the 2017/2021 tomato policy and helped push for increased credit risk guarantees (30% to 50%) for plastic crates, and supported the rollout of frameworks for organic agriculture" ; Said the unpredictability deterred young people from seeking jobs in horticulture, which erodes the sector's long-term sustainability and threatens national food supply plans.

a1164.speaker: HortiNigeria programme (recommendations)
a1164.name: HortiNigeria programme (recommendations)
a1164.speech: Proposed practical solutions: "Stakeholders should expand access to solar-powered irrigation systems and localised weather forecasting tools, especially for smallholders..." ; "Federal and state governments, with private sector partners, should prioritise the deployment of low-cost storage solutions, such as Zero Energy Cool Chambers (ZECC) and upgrade cold chain logistics nationwide. Additionally, incentives should be given to local processors to absorb tomato surpluses, stabilising demand during harvest peaks." ; "Real-time price dissemination should be scaled up by FMAFS through a dedicated horticulture desk within the Ministry of Agriculture, transitioning HortiNigeria's efforts beyond social media to include SMS-based alerts, radio broadcasts and community price boards in key markets." ; "Institutions like NIHORT should expand community-based demonstration plots and training on IPM practices, particularly for women and youth groups. Agro-dealer networks should be strengthened and monitored to ensure availability and affordability of bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and safe chemical alternatives." ; "To mitigate labour shortages, especially in southern states, stakeholders should promote labour cooperatives and deploy subsidised mechanisation hubs offering shared access to harvesters and planters." ; "To support the implementation of the national strategy on tuta absoluta and reduce price volatility, a centralised data system managed by the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security should be established..."

a1164.speaker: Alhaji Abdullahi Ringim, national president, Tomato Out-growers Association of Nigeria (TOGAN)
a1164.name: Alhaji Abdullahi Ringim
a1164.title: national president, Tomato Out-growers Association of Nigeria (TOGAN)
a1164.speech: In an earlier conversation with Daily Trust, estimated that farmers lost more than N1.7 billion in 2023.

a1164.speaker: Alhaji Sani Danladi Yadakwari, chairman of TOGAN in Kano State
a1164.name: Alhaji Sani Danladi Yadakwari
a1164.title: chairman of TOGAN in Kano State
a1164.speech: Provided comparable estimations; he said that tuta absoluta attacked and damaged more than N1.5 billion worth of tomato plants this year.

a1164.speaker: Mohammed Salasi Idris, programme director of HortiNigeria
a1164.name: Mohammed Salasi Idris
a1164.title: programme director of HortiNigeria
a1164.speech: In a recent presentation in Abuja, said the project was working with Eupepsia Place and NIHORT to upgrade cold storage facilities in Ogun and Oyo and install local Zero Energy Cool Chambers (ZECC) in Kaduna and Kano.

a1164.speaker: Stakeholders in the Nigerian tomato sector
a1164.name: Stakeholders in the Nigerian tomato sector
a1164.speech: Reckoned that farmers who don't have access to enough storage facilities are frequently compelled to sell their tomatoes at a loss when prices drop significantly after harvest, and that they might have little to no produce remaining to profit from growing prices during times of shortage.

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “It is very important to invite the United States Chamber of Commerce to invest in ports, roads and logistics infrastructure. Beira is our main point for the outflow of oil and a vital corridor for international trade routes.” ; “Mozambique has everything it needs to become a relevant economic actor in Southern Africa. We have a strategic location, access to the sea and borders with six countries. What we need now is investment in roads, ports, railways and modern logistics systems that connect markets and boost regional trade.”

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “We have coal, graphite, gold and many critical minerals. But the most important thing is to transform these resources into concrete opportunities that create jobs and generate value for the Mozambican people,” stressing that the objective is to industrialise the country and promote a more diversified and competitive economy.

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: Highlighted that Mozambique is investing in large power generation plants, including Mphanda Nkuwa, Cahora Bassa and Temane, which together could supply thousands of megawatts to the national grid and to neighbouring countries: “We want not only to strengthen the quantity and quality of electricity in the country, but also to export it to the whole region,” recalling that Mozambique is the only SADC country with real capacity to respond to the energy deficit affecting Zambia, Malawi, Zimbabwe and South Africa.

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “We have assets, we have demand in the region, but we need financing. That is why we are here, in the United States, which is one of the world’s greatest references in financing megaprojects.” ; “This visit was not merely symbolic. We came to work, to deliver, so that Mozambique stops being just a supplier and becomes a protagonist.”

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “The world has a food deficit problem. Mozambique can be part of the solution, if it invests in agriculture and agro-processing. We want to industrialise the country, generate jobs for young people and for women, and transform the agricultural sector into an engine of our growth.”

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “They were impressed to learn that the Aman group, one of the ten largest hotel groups in the world, chose Mozambique for its first entry into sub-Saharan Africa,” and invited new investors to take part in the International Tourism Conference scheduled for 3 and 4 November in Vilankulo.

a1251.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1251.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1251.title: President of Mozambique
a1251.speech: “What we are doing now is the complete digitalisation of State services. We want to eliminate corruption and create clarity in all administrative and financial procedures. Predictability is essential for business.”

a1352.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1352.name: Donald Trump
a1352.title: US President
a1352.speech: Riding to power for the second time on the mantra of "America First," vowed to shut the country's borders to illegal migrants; even since the time of his first presidential campaign in 2016, Trump has strongly and repeatedly emphasized a need to safeguard the interests of the US by adopting policies that would firmly place "America First".

a1352.speaker: Trump's detractors
a1352.name: Trump's detractors
a1352.speech: Are condemning his deportation strategies, pointing out that they could usher in an era of human rights violations as well as large-scale trauma which could affect families and communities more likely to be targeted by mass deportations.

a1352.speaker: Some experts
a1352.name: Some experts
a1352.speech: Argue that mass deportations could benefit American workers by raising wages and improving job conditions.

a1352.speaker: Other experts
a1352.name: Other experts
a1352.speech: Have warned that plans to remove millions of working immigrants have the potential to hasten economic instability, especially as cheap immigrant labour helps key sectors like agriculture and hospitality.

a1352.speaker: Migration Policy Institute (database)
a1352.name: Migration Policy Institute (database)
a1352.speech: Cited as the source for the figures that Biden carried out deportations with about 271,000 immigrants flown out to approximately 192 countries in just 2024, and a total of 1.5 million illegal immigrants deported during his four years as the 46th President.

a1352.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1352.name: Donald Trump
a1352.title: US President
a1352.speech: In a televised moment during one of his debates with then Democratic presidential candidate and former Vice President Kamala Harris, blamed a wave of Haitian immigrants for the deaths of domesticated animals in Springfield, Ohio; although this claim was refuted as baseless and false, Trump has not backed down from constantly pointing out that illegal immigration poses a huge threat not just to the economy of the US, but to the security of its cities and citizens.

a1352.speaker: Punch Newspaper (report)
a1352.name: Punch Newspaper (report)
a1352.speech: According to a recent report by Punch Newspaper, US-based Nigerians have gone into hiding amid Trump's deportation crackdown. Many have stopped going to churches, mosques, and even their workplaces, fearing they could be the next targets.

a1352.speaker: A Life Bencher, Body of Benchers, Nigerian Law School (unnamed)
a1352.name: A Life Bencher
a1352.title: Body of Benchers, Nigerian Law School (unnamed)
a1352.speech: Echoed the sentiment that this country is all we have, at a recent law dinner with the Body of Benchers at the Nigerian Law School, Bwari.

a1382.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a1382.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a1382.title: Namibian Health Minister
a1382.speech: Said the recent executive order signed by United States president Donald Trump to withdraw funding from the World Health Organisation (WHO) will likely not affect Namibia, due to bilateral relations and existing projects between the two states. "Namibia has bilateral funding agreements with the US in the health sector for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and other diseases around advocacy, prevention and treatment through the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), Centres for Disease Control (CDC) and others. We expect that these bilateral programmes will not be affected." ; added that "all Namibian health programmes are funded by the government, and development partners' contributions amount to 30% of funding".

a1382.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a1382.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a1382.title: Namibian Health Minister
a1382.speech: Told New Era that the US is one of the major funders of the WHO and that the withdrawal will result in reduced funding for the WHO, which will negatively impact the organisation's operations. He reiterated that, as it happened in the past, the WHO will work with member states to minimise the negative impact of this withdrawal by mobilising additional resources. "Already during the 75th World Health Assembly, member states of the WHO took a historic decision to sustainably finance the WHO. In this regard, member states agreed to a gradual increase in their assessed contributions to represent at least 50% of WHO's core budget by the 2030-2031 budget cycle."

a1382.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a1382.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a1382.title: Namibian Health Minister
a1382.speech: Noted that the WHO has done commendable work in supporting member states to manage health challenges through technical support, especially the developing countries. "Here, in Namibia, the WHO supported the Ministry of Health and Social Services during the plague outbreak in the early nineties and polio in the mid-twenties – just to mention a few. The WHO is indispensable in the contemporary world, where no country is safe from a health emergency if one country is afflicted by that health emergency."

a1382.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1382.name: Donald Trump
a1382.title: President of the United States
a1382.speech: At his inauguration as Head of State, said the US will leave the organisation. He added that the global health agency mishandled the Covid-19 pandemic and other international health crises. Trump said the WHO had failed to act independently from the "inappropriate political influence" of its member states. He said it required "unfairly onerous payments" from the US, which were disproportionate to the sums provided by other, larger countries, such as China.

a1382.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO director general
a1382.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a1382.title: WHO director general
a1382.speech: Said they regret the announcement that the US intends to withdraw from the organisation. "We hope the US will reconsider. We look forward to engaging in constructive dialogue to maintain the partnership between the USA and the WHO." He added that the WHO plays a crucial role in protecting the health and security of the world's people, including Americans, by addressing the root causes of disease, building stronger health systems as well as detecting, preventing and responding to health emergencies, including disease outbreaks, often in dangerous places where others cannot go.

a1382.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a1382.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a1382.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a1382.speech: Was dismayed to learn of the US government's announcement to withdraw from the WHO. "The US, as a member of WHO, was crucial in shaping global WHO instruments and norms on public health security and well-being over the past seven decades." He said in Africa, the US was an early and strong supporter of the establishment of the Africa CDC, the African Union's technical agency for public health emergencies. "Today, now more than ever, the world depends on the WHO to carry out its mandate to ensure global public health security as a shared common good. I hope the US government will reconsider its decision to withdraw from this key global organisation, of which it is a founding member."

a1452.speaker: Professor Obert Jiri, Permanent Secretary for Zimbabwe's Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development
a1452.name: Professor Obert Jiri
a1452.title: Permanent Secretary for Zimbabwe's Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development
a1452.speech: Described the launch as a "defining moment" in regional collaboration: "It is a great pleasure to inaugurate these two projects which embody our shared vision as Zimbabwe and Mozambique. These are not merely development projects, they are strategic instruments to unlock economic growth and to urgently restore our Miombo forests." ; Emphasized the need to combat unsustainable land use, deforestation, and climate change, which have long threatened the integrity of the Miombo ecosystem: "Today is a day to challenge these challenges through collaboration, through innovation, and through unity of purpose."

a1452.speaker: Gustavo Sorbhino Dgedge, Mozambican Secretary of State for Land and Environment
a1452.name: Gustavo Sorbhino Dgedge
a1452.title: Mozambican Secretary of State for Land and Environment
a1452.speech: Expressed gratitude to Zimbabwe for hosting the event and to Italy for financing the initiatives: "On behalf of the Government of Mozambique and on my own behalf, I say thank you. This initiative will contribute significantly towards our National Forestry Program 2037 and is perfectly aligned with Mozambique's goals under the Southern African Development Community (SADC) free trade area." ; Underlined the transformative ecological implications of the forestry project for his country: "This will enable us to better monitor cross-border forest resource movements and enforce more robust surveillance systems. We are pleased to see our delegates working shoulder to shoulder to protect our shared environment."

a1452.speaker: Umberto Malnati, Italian Ambassador to Zimbabwe
a1452.name: Umberto Malnati
a1452.title: Italian Ambassador to Zimbabwe
a1452.speech: Hailed the initiative as a testament to what strong partnerships can achieve: "The success of these initiatives depends on the strength of the partnership between Zimbabwe and Mozambique. Italy is proud to be supporting these visionary efforts. These two countries are strategic partners to us, and we appreciate the way this support has been received." ; Emphasized the inclusive nature of the projects, saying they will promote agro-processing and prioritize participation of women and youth in marginalized communities, especially in rural areas where the projects will be implemented.

a1593.speaker: French Ministry of the Interior
a1593.name: French Ministry of the Interior
a1593.speech: explained that the curfew will be in place from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m. local time for security reasons, in order to prevent looting ; according to the Interior Ministry, 50% of running water will be restored within 48 hours.

a1593.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a1593.name: Emmanuel Macron
a1593.title: President of France
a1593.speech: "Faced with this tragedy which upsets each of us, I will decree a period of national mourning," Mr Macron announced on Monday evening, adding that he would go "in the coming days" to Mayotte "in support" of the population and of all those mobilised.

a1593.speaker: French authorities
a1593.name: French authorities
a1593.speech: The authorities fear "several hundred" deaths, perhaps even "a few thousand", in this poorest department of France.

a1593.speaker: Bruno Retailleau, French Interior Minister
a1593.name: Bruno Retailleau
a1593.title: French Interior Minister
a1593.speech: "The toll will be heavy, too heavy," warned on Monday ; "The island is totally devastated," he explained from La Réunion, specifying that "70% of the inhabitants have been severely affected" ; announced the arrival "in the coming days" of 400 additional gendarmes to support the 1,600 gendarmes and police present on the archipelago, while specifying that there had "not really been any looting" so far ; insisted that the priority is to ensure the "vital needs" of residents in water and food ; indicated that the only hospital, badly damaged, "is gradually resuming its activity" and will be supported by a field hospital from Thursday.

a1593.speaker: Bruno Retailleau, French Interior Minister
a1593.name: Bruno Retailleau
a1593.title: French Interior Minister
a1593.speech: has already stressed that the Mayotte archipelago cannot be rebuilt "without dealing with the migration question".

a1593.speaker: Antoy Abdallah, 34, resident of Tsoundzou
a1593.name: Antoy Abdallah
a1593.title: 34, resident of Tsoundzou
a1593.speech: "We are starting to run out of water. We have a few bottles left but there is almost no stock left in the shops," he told AFP with concern ; "We are completely cut off from the world. We have access to no information."

a1593.speaker: Ben Issa Ousseni, president of the departmental council of Mayotte
a1593.name: Ben Issa Ousseni
a1593.title: president of the departmental council of Mayotte
a1593.speech: "We risk a health crisis," he warned.

a1593.speaker: Geneviève Darrieussecq, French Health Minister
a1593.name: Geneviève Darrieussecq
a1593.title: French Health Minister
a1593.speech: said the situation of the care system is "very degraded" in Mayotte.

a1593.speaker: French Red Cross
a1593.name: French Red Cross
a1593.speech: According to the French Red Cross, 20 tonnes of equipment are being shipped.

a1593.speaker: François Bayrou, new French Prime Minister
a1593.name: François Bayrou
a1593.title: new French Prime Minister
a1593.speech: called for "national solidarity" on Monday evening, from his municipal council in Pau, in south-western France.

a1593.speaker: Yaël Braun-Pivet, President of the French National Assembly
a1593.name: Yaël Braun-Pivet
a1593.title: President of the French National Assembly
a1593.speech: stated on Tuesday morning that she would have "preferred that the Prime Minister take the plane to Mayotte".

a1593.speaker: National Institute of Statistics (INSEE)
a1593.name: National Institute of Statistics (INSEE)
a1593.speech: According to the National Institute of Statistics, nearly half of the population is made up of immigrants who came from the neighbouring Comoros or other African countries.

a1593.speaker: Marc Ferracci, French Industry Minister
a1593.name: Marc Ferracci
a1593.title: French Industry Minister
a1593.speech: lamented that a large part of the archipelago is still without electricity, mobile network and internet, which are nevertheless "priorities to allow security and economic recovery".

a1593.speaker: City of Mamoudzou (capital of Mayotte)
a1593.name: City of Mamoudzou (capital of Mayotte)
a1593.speech: called on Monday for its adult residents in "good physical condition" to "reinforce the teams on the ground".

a1593.speaker: United States
a1593.name: United States
a1593.speech: indicated it was ready to "offer appropriate humanitarian aid".

a1645.speaker: Aid groups
a1645.name: Aid groups
a1645.speech: call the situation the world's worst humanitarian crisis, with tens of thousands of people killed or injured and about 13 million uprooted since April 2023.

a1645.speaker: Tariq Ahmed, 56, Khartoum resident
a1645.name: Tariq Ahmed
a1645.title: 56, Khartoum resident
a1645.speech: "Khartoum is not habitable. The war has destroyed our life and our country and we feel homeless even though the army is back in control."

a1645.speaker: Sudanese authorities
a1645.name: Sudanese authorities
a1645.speech: estimate reconstruction needs at $300 billion for Khartoum and $700 billion for the rest of Sudan; authorities estimate hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of reconstruction would be needed.

a1645.speaker: Mohieddine Naeem, Sudanese Oil and Energy Minister
a1645.name: Mohieddine Naeem
a1645.title: Sudanese Oil and Energy Minister
a1645.speech: told Reuters that Sudan's oil production has more than halved to 24,000 barrels-per-day and its refining capabilities ceased as the main al-Jaili oil refinery sustained $3 billion in damages during battles ; said that without refining capacity, Sudan now exports all its crude and relies on imports, and that it also struggles to maintain pipelines needed by South Sudan for its own exports ; said all of Khartoum's power stations have been destroyed.

a1645.speaker: Sudan (government)
a1645.name: Sudan (government)
a1645.speech: blamed the UAE for drone attacks that targeted fuel depots and the airport at the country's main port city.

a1645.speaker: Sudan's national electrical company
a1645.name: Sudan's national electrical company
a1645.speech: recently announced a plan to increase supply from Egypt to northern Sudan and said earlier in the year that repeated drone attacks to stations outside Khartoum were stretching its ability to keep the grid going.

a1645.speaker: Altayeb Saadeddine, Khartoum state spokesperson
a1645.name: Altayeb Saadeddine
a1645.title: Khartoum state spokesperson
a1645.speech: said Khartoum's two main water stations went out of commission early in the war as RSF soldiers looted machinery and used fuel oil to power vehicles.

a1645.speaker: Haitham Mohamed Ibrahim, Sudanese Health Minister
a1645.name: Haitham Mohamed Ibrahim
a1645.title: Sudanese Health Minister
a1645.speech: "There has been systematic sabotage by militias against hospitals, and most medical equipment has been looted and what remains has been deliberately destroyed," putting losses to the health system at $11 billion.

a1645.speaker: Luca Renda, United Nations Development Programme resident representative
a1645.name: Luca Renda
a1645.title: United Nations Development Programme resident representative
a1645.speech: said that with two or three million people looking at returning to Khartoum, interventions were needed to avoid further humanitarian emergencies like the cholera outbreak ; "What we can do … with the capacity we have on the ground, is to look at smaller-scale infrastructure rehabilitation," like solar-power water pumps, hospitals, and schools ; said the war may in that way provide an opportunity for decentralising services away from Khartoum, and pursuing greener energy sources.

a1764.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.name: Lauren Greubel
a1764.title: Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.speech: In her speech, emphasised the importance of preschool education as an essential foundation for children's futures. She further highlighted the multiple benefits that allow pupils to develop early skills, to be better prepared for primary school, and to significantly reduce the risks of dropping out of school.

a1764.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.name: Lauren Greubel
a1764.title: Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.speech: Addressing in particular the children who had just started school: "I am delighted by the adventure you are embarking on. School is a place for fun, for making friends, for singing songs, and for learning about your country and the world. You have the support of your parents, your teachers, your communities, the government and USAID," she declared, before praising the efforts of the 'Play to Learn' programme teams and of the actors involved, affirming that their dedication is a source of inspiration for building a promising future for the children of Djibouti.

a1764.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.name: Lauren Greubel
a1764.title: Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a1764.speech: "The Djiboutian government is making considerable efforts to offer every child the right to a quality education." ; "USAID's project 'Play to Learn' aims to increase the number of children benefiting from a quality education. A quality, inclusive preschool education can have a significant impact on children's learning outcomes for the rest of their lives. Preschool programmes offer many benefits to pupils, their families and their communities. Pupils develop early academic skills and are better prepared to enter primary school. The data has shown that when children attend preschool, they are more likely to complete secondary school, their dropout rate is reduced, and their learning outcomes are better. Through the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training and the Ministry of Women and Family, the Djiboutian government is making considerable efforts to find lasting solutions to offer every child, and particularly children in vulnerable situations, the right to a quality education."

a1764.speaker: Fozia Ibrahim, Head of the Preschool Service of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1764.name: Fozia Ibrahim
a1764.title: Head of the Preschool Service of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1764.speech: For her part, highlighted the importance of this partnership for strengthening the capacities of private preschool establishments, but also reminded parents of the importance of monitoring their children's attendance.

a2069.speaker: Government of Botswana
a2069.name: Government of Botswana
a2069.speech: Announced on Wednesday that the United States has suspended, with immediate effect, its aid to the health sector, jeopardising crucial programmes, particularly in the fight against HIV/AIDS.

a2069.speaker: Dr Christopher Nyanga, spokesperson for the Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.name: Dr Christopher Nyanga
a2069.title: spokesperson for the Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.speech: Said the aid "was decisive in making Botswana one of the first countries in the world to reach and exceed UNAIDS' 95-95-95 targets."

a2069.speaker: Dr Christopher Nyanga, spokesperson for the Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.name: Dr Christopher Nyanga
a2069.title: spokesperson for the Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.speech: Added that the authorities are planning discussions with the US embassy to "hold a dialogue on how the affected services can be maintained."

a2069.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.name: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a2069.speech: Assures that the supply of antiretroviral medicines is not under threat, as it is directly covered by the Botswanan government.

a2127.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a2127.name: David Stevenson
a2127.title: WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a2127.speech: "The African Development Bank's support is timely and comes as a lifeline for those struggling to feed themselves amidst rising food prices and economic turmoil." ; "Communities which, after years of conflict and violence, started rebuilding their lives were struck by the floods and once again displaced, meaning more and more people cannot support themselves and their families."

a2127.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024)
a2127.name: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024)
a2127.speech: Projects that 33 million people in Nigeria will face food insecurity by August 2025.

a2127.speaker: Abdul Kamara, African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a2127.name: Abdul Kamara
a2127.title: African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a2127.speech: "I hope that this additional funding will mitigate the suffering of vulnerable people on the brink of acute hunger at a time when more Nigerians than ever need humanitarian assistance." ; "I commend the Federal Government of Nigeria and WFP for the continuous efforts to operate in such a challenging environment to improve the lives of Nigerian families."

a2323.speaker: Prosper Africa Tech for Trade Alliance
a2323.name: Prosper Africa Tech for Trade Alliance
a2323.speech: Announced on 12 November a pharmaceutical tracing pilot project in South Africa as part of the US Digital Transformation with Africa (DTA) strategy, under which Prosper Africa, USAID's e-Trade Alliance, IBM and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy will test a solution to transform African pharmaceutical markets.

a2323.speaker: British Robinson, coordinator of Prosper Africa
a2323.name: British Robinson
a2323.title: coordinator of Prosper Africa
a2323.speech: "Through Prosper Africa's Tech for Trade Alliance, under the Digital Trade for Africa (DTA) initiative, we are supporting business-to-business partnerships to leverage technology and create products/services that catalyse financial and social returns for Africans and Americans. We are delighted that IBM is using its Watson AI capabilities in this pilot project to help improve the traceability of medicines exported to Africa."

a2362.speaker: Civil society groups
a2362.name: Civil society groups
a2362.speech: Accuse authorities of stifling dissent over a policy critics say prioritizes telecom profits over public welfare.

a2362.speaker: Assan Martin, lawyer representing the detainees
a2362.name: Assan Martin
a2362.title: lawyer representing the detainees
a2362.speech: Described the arrests as "illegal and unacceptable", noting that while bail was offered for Friday detainees, the conditions were overly restrictive, requiring a surety.

a2362.speaker: Gambians Against Looted Assets (GALA) (statement)
a2362.name: Gambians Against Looted Assets (GALA) (statement)
a2362.speech: Statement on Saturday underscored this resolve: "They have collectively and unequivocally refused to accept the terms of their release, choosing to remain in detention rather than comply with excessively restrictive and unjust demands."

a2362.speaker: Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA)
a2362.name: Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA)
a2362.speech: Defends the D50 per gigabyte price floor, citing network congestion and the need for sustainable investment.

a2362.speaker: Gambia Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
a2362.name: Gambia Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
a2362.speech: Argues the price floor burdens low-income households.

a2362.speaker: Yusef Taylor, activist
a2362.name: Yusef Taylor
a2362.title: activist
a2362.speech: Said before his arrest: "This price floor is a betrayal of the Gambian people," highlighting its impact on education, employment, and civic engagement.

a2362.speaker: Solo Sandeng Foundation
a2362.name: Solo Sandeng Foundation
a2362.speech: Condemned the arrests, invoking the memory of the activist murdered in 2016 for protesting: "It is unacceptable that young people are still arrested for exercising their constitutional rights," the Foundation stated, demanding the detainees immediate release and a review of PURA policy.

a2712.speaker: Coordination Unit for the formulation of the 2nd programme and the monitoring of reforms of MCA-Benin (UCF/MCA-Benin), press briefing
a2712.name: Coordination Unit for the formulation of the 2nd programme and the monitoring of reforms of MCA-Benin (UCF/MCA-Benin)
a2712.title: press briefing
a2712.speech: confirmed Benin's eligibility for the 2nd MCC compact and presented the content of the programme for the coming five years as well as the benefits Benin can draw from it.

a2712.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.name: Samuel Batcho
a2712.title: national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.speech: expressed the Beninese government's gratitude to the American people and to their government, and praised the diplomatic skill of the United States ambassador to Benin in bringing this matter to a successful conclusion.

a2712.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.name: Samuel Batcho
a2712.title: national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.speech: recalled that it was the corruption indicator that was in the red, causing the country to be turned down, and that the decision was taken unanimously last year; but this year, thanks to the progress made by everyone and above all the anti-corruption plan put in place by the government, the country reached this positive result. Benin had never before passed more than 11 indicators; this year it passed 12. "If everyone does their part, if there are greater efforts, Benin can pass 13 or even 14 indicators."

a2712.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.name: Samuel Batcho
a2712.title: national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin
a2712.speech: on the amount of the funds: "A base envelope of 250 million US dollars," specifying that Ghana had a base envelope of 300 million dollars, but with the flexibility of the Americans and the support of its private sector the envelope rose to 500 million US dollars. "Benin can do just as much. It all depends on us."

a2712.speaker: The speakers at the press conference (UCF/MCA-Benin and MCC officials)
a2712.name: The speakers at the press conference (UCF/MCA-Benin and MCC officials)
a2712.speech: said the Programme will be exclusively concentrated on the energy sector in Benin, a sector they describe as strategic for the country's development ; assured that feasibility studies will be carried out.

a2712.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.name: Jonathan Bloom
a2712.title: MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.speech: "If we can supply more electricity, that can unleash the engine of growth in Benin"; underlined the need to build an attractive framework in order to attract investment from everyone. "That will require enormous efforts on the part of the MCC and commitments on the part of the government of Benin." He added that he hopes this will help make the dreams of the Beninese people last. ; "There are today new technologies that can help reduce electricity consumption. If a stable institutional framework is put in place, that can attract the private sector."

a2712.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.name: Jonathan Bloom
a2712.title: MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.speech: invited everyone to make progress and to go beyond the progress achieved by Ghana, and said he hopes the private sector will seize the opportunity to do as the Ghanaians did.

a2712.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.name: Jonathan Bloom
a2712.title: MCC deputy vice-president
a2712.speech: on the MCC's motivation in signing the compact with Benin, specified that it is "just so that there may be a more just, freer and more prosperous world. That is the whole interest of the USA."

a2749.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Ethiopian Finance Minister
a2749.name: Ahmed Shide
a2749.title: Ethiopian Finance Minister
a2749.speech: Emphasised the need to reprioritise federal expenditures despite the proposed budget bill being nearly 112 billion Br higher than what had been apportioned for this fiscal year: “The fiscal space that allowed the government to provide financing for development objectives is narrowing,” the Finance Minister told legislators. ; Cautioned Parliamentarians that the budget bill would suffice only if the existing tenuous peace is sustained, repeating the point three times ; Conceded that financing the bloated budget through the mobilisation of domestic revenues will be testing: “Over a quarter of the tax revenue planned for this year will not be collected,” the Finance Minister admitted ; On deficit financing through treasury bills: “There's no better alternative” ; Warned of the hardships ahead: “It's essential to use the available financial resource to the best of our abilities,” he told legislators. “This is the most important task awaiting the country.”

a2749.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (PhD), professor of economics at Addis Abeba University
a2749.name: Alemayehu Geda (PhD)
a2749.title: professor of economics at Addis Abeba University
a2749.speech: Said the growing share of recurrent expenditure shows that the focus is on sustaining the economy by covering administrative expenses ; Argued that the overall budget adjustment is insignificant when calculated in dollar terms, with the budget bill exhibiting a 14pc rise in dollar terms ; Sees other options, such as infrastructure bonds, and warns that the administration might turn its attention to direct borrowing from the central bank if financing the budget deficit through T-bills becomes unattainable: “This has been the trend in the past,” he said.

a2749.speaker: Christian Tadelle, opposition legislator from the National Movement of Amhara (NAMA)
a2749.name: Christian Tadelle
a2749.title: opposition legislator from the National Movement of Amhara (NAMA)
a2749.speech: “The government should first ensure that citizens are well fed,” said Christian Tadelle, as MPs raised concerns over the expenditure budgeted for the defence forces.

a2749.speaker: Arega Shumetie (PhD), senior researcher at the Ethiopian Economics Association
a2749.name: Arega Shumetie (PhD)
a2749.title: senior researcher at the Ethiopian Economics Association
a2749.speech: “They can broaden the tax base instead of introducing new categories,” he said of officials' plans to introduce new forms of taxes including a property tax ; On the administration's 10-year target to collect 2.6 trillion Br in annual tax: “The target ignores the reality on the ground.”

a2749.speaker: Administration officials (Ethiopian federal government)
a2749.name: Administration officials (Ethiopian federal government)
a2749.speech: Argue that the budget is an expression of their objective to ensure reconstruction in the north damaged by the civil war ; Urged federal agencies during the federal budget hearings last month to slash expenditures for the next year ; Projected the deficit to reach 3.5pc of GDP, and urge that they are determined to avoid direct borrowing from the central bank in fear of exasperating inflation ; Plan to introduce new forms of taxes, including a property tax.

a2749.speaker: Cepheus Capital, private equity firm (forecast)
a2749.name: Cepheus Capital
a2749.title: private equity firm (forecast)
a2749.speech: Forecast a budget deficit for the coming fiscal year five percentage points higher than the administration's projection of 3.5pc of GDP.

a2895.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2895.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2895.speech: Announced a temporary suspension of $125.5 million in aid to Somalia, a decision which excludes funding for Israel and Egypt.

a2895.speaker: Somalia's leaders and aid organizations
a2895.name: Somalia's leaders and aid organizations
a2895.speech: Are scrambling to find alternative funding sources while urging the U.S. government to reconsider.

a2895.speaker: Ken Jackson, senior USAID official (internal memo to USAID staff)
a2895.name: Ken Jackson
a2895.title: senior USAID official (internal memo to USAID staff)
a2895.speech: Emphasized that the freeze marked “a complete halt” in funding, with waivers requiring high-level approval.

a2895.speaker: Humanitarian organizations
a2895.name: Humanitarian organizations
a2895.speech: Caught off guard by the abrupt freeze, warn of dire consequences.

a2895.speaker: Abby Maxman, president of Oxfam America
a2895.name: Abby Maxman
a2895.title: president of Oxfam America
a2895.speech: “It's a cruel and dangerous decision,” said Abby Maxman, president of Oxfam America. “Millions of lives are at stake as these critical services grind to a halt.”

a3013.speaker: Federal Government of Somalia
a3013.name: Federal Government of Somalia
a3013.speech: Announced that it had, in collaboration with U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM), successfully executed an airstrike against ISIS militants who were congregating in the southeastern area of Bosasso, Puntland, bolstering the efforts of Puntland Darwish forces ; Stated that it remains committed, with the support of international partners like AFRICOM, to combating terrorist organizations such as ISIS and Al-Shabaab, which pose significant threats to both national and global security.

a3013.speaker: Preliminary evaluations (of the airstrike)
a3013.name: Preliminary evaluations (of the airstrike)
a3013.speech: Suggest that multiple ISIS fighters were neutralized, with no reported civilian casualties.

a3101.speaker: Sarah Williams, 33-year-old South Sudanese refugee and mother of five
a3101.name: Sarah Williams
a3101.title: 33-year-old South Sudanese refugee and mother of five
a3101.speech: “We were crawling on the ground,” she recalls of the fighting reaching her Khartoum neighbourhood. “It was chaos.” ; “The conflict started among themselves. But later, they began killing South Sudanese also, even though we weren’t part of their fight.”

a3101.speaker: Sarah Williams, South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.name: Sarah Williams
a3101.title: South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.speech: “There’s conflict ahead of us,” she tells the BBC, explaining she cannot travel to her hometown of Nasir. ; “I don’t know where they ran to when the clashes started… or even if they’re alive.”

a3101.speaker: Sarah Williams, South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.name: Sarah Williams
a3101.title: South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.speech: “I used to collect firewood and sell it to buy flour, but there’s nothing left in the forest now. No wood for women to collect and sell.”

a3101.speaker: Sarah Williams, South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.name: Sarah Williams
a3101.title: South Sudanese refugee stranded in Renk
a3101.speech: Says she has no intention of going back to Khartoum, and has decided that it is best to try and rebuild her life in her home country, “even if the situation is bad”.

a3101.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a3101.name: United Nations (UN)
a3101.speech: Warning that the 2018 peace agreement between Kiir and Machar is at risk of collapsing.

a3101.speaker: Aid agencies
a3101.name: Aid agencies
a3101.speech: Say Sudan’s conflict has caused the world’s biggest humanitarian crisis.

a3101.speaker: Vijaya Souri, International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3101.name: Vijaya Souri
a3101.title: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3101.speech: Says aid agencies are scrambling to move families to safer parts of South Sudan, where people have “stronger community or family ties, livelihood opportunities, and better access to services”.

a3101.speaker: Mary Deng, refugee who escaped from Wad Madani
a3101.name: Mary Deng
a3101.title: refugee who escaped from Wad Madani
a3101.speech: “This child was just one day old when we crossed the border. We are 16 in total. We had no money - but we had God.”

a3101.speaker: Health worker at the Joda border clinic (anonymous)
a3101.name: Health worker at the Joda border clinic (anonymous)
a3101.speech: “Over 600 babies have been born here since the war began. But we can only operate during the day now, there’s no funding for night shifts.”

a3101.speaker: Tatek Wondimu Mamecha, World Health Organisation (WHO) emergency officer in South Sudan
a3101.name: Tatek Wondimu Mamecha
a3101.title: World Health Organisation (WHO) emergency officer in South Sudan
a3101.speech: Warns of the growing risks: “Even though the cholera outbreak is controlled, we’re not out of the woods. Right now, malaria is spiking and with the rainy season coming, it will shoot up.”

a3101.speaker: Tatek Wondimu Mamecha, World Health Organisation (WHO) emergency officer in South Sudan
a3101.name: Tatek Wondimu Mamecha
a3101.title: World Health Organisation (WHO) emergency officer in South Sudan
