a3101.speech: Adds that the ripple effects of global aid cuts by US President Donald Trump’s administration are devastating: “Five of our partners either stopped service or reduced operations by 50%.” ; “The facility manages around 350 to 400 patients a day,” he says of Renk Referral hospital, which has lost half its staff.

a3101.speaker: George Owino, chair of the monitoring body set up under the 2018 peace deal
a3101.name: George Owino
a3101.title: chair of the monitoring body set up under the 2018 peace deal
a3101.speech: Has warned that the latest clashes “threaten the foundation of the agreement.”

a3101.speaker: George Owino, chair of the monitoring body set up under the 2018 peace deal
a3101.name: George Owino
a3101.title: chair of the monitoring body set up under the 2018 peace deal
a3101.speech: Tells the BBC the core problem is that political leaders continue to command rival troops, failing to integrate them into a unified national army: “The link between politics and military power is still intact. When leaders disagree, it quickly turns into armed confrontation - exactly what the agreement was supposed to prevent.” ; “There used to be more dialogue within the presidency. That has diminished.”

a3101.speaker: Machar’s party (SPLM-IO)
a3101.name: Machar’s party (SPLM-IO)
a3101.speech: Denies the claim by Kiir’s allies that Machar supported armed groups.

a3101.speaker: Machar’s party (SPLM-IO)
a3101.name: Machar’s party (SPLM-IO)
a3101.speech: Says the Ugandan troop deployment undermines South Sudan’s sovereignty, and the 2018 peace deal.

a3101.speaker: Uganda and Kiir’s government
a3101.name: Uganda and Kiir’s government
a3101.speech: Both defend the deployment, saying it is in accordance with a long-standing security agreement between the two nations.

a3101.speaker: Gen Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti), Rapid Support Forces leader
a3101.name: Gen Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti)
a3101.title: Rapid Support Forces leader
a3101.speech: Announcing the formation of a rival government in Sudan.

a3101.speaker: Salva Kiir, South Sudanese President
a3101.name: Salva Kiir
a3101.title: South Sudanese President
a3101.speech: Sacked Machar as vice-president in 2013, accusing him of plotting a coup.

a3101.speaker: Riek Machar, South Sudanese opposition leader
a3101.name: Riek Machar
a3101.title: South Sudanese opposition leader
a3101.speech: Made the counter-accusation that Kiir was a “dictator”.

a3160.speaker: Marcelo Ramirez, analyst
a3160.name: Marcelo Ramirez
a3160.title: analyst
a3160.speech: calls this new order "The obsolescence of classical ideologies."

a3160.speaker: FBI (informally)
a3160.name: FBI (informally)
a3160.speech: secretly calls Donald Trump "Putin's orange agent."

a3160.speaker: Alain Charles Martinet, management scholar ("Strategy and complex thought", Revue francaise de gestion, No 93, 1993; "Research in strategy: a problem of granularity", No 256, 2016)
a3160.name: Alain Charles Martinet
a3160.title: management scholar ("Strategy and complex thought", Revue francaise de gestion, No 93, 1993; "Research in strategy: a problem of granularity", No 256, 2016)
a3160.speech: "a winning culture can raise strategy to unsuspected heights" ; "strategy is thought and put into action because situations pose problems" ; argues that strategy calls for complex thought.

a3160.speaker: Pierre Bourdieu, sociologist
a3160.name: Pierre Bourdieu
a3160.title: sociologist
a3160.speech: had explained as far back as 1998, recalling that the triumph of neoliberalism would depend on its capacity to destroy the collective structures that can resist and obstruct the logic of the pure market.

a3160.speaker: Albert Camus, writer
a3160.name: Albert Camus
a3160.title: writer
a3160.speech: had suggested that "everything that degrades culture is a shortcut to barbarism."

a3160.speaker: Soufyane Frimousse ("Tame the unforeseeable and the uncertain", 2022, EMS)
a3160.name: Soufyane Frimousse ("Tame the unforeseeable and the uncertain"
a3160.title: 2022, EMS)
a3160.speech: cited for the claim that each wave of turbulence contains both uncertainties and lines of flight towards states of equilibrium adapted to the disturbances which, because they move away from the known, open the way to the unknown, source of innovation and of the unhoped-for.

a3160.speaker: J.D. Vance, US Vice-President, Donald Trump's right-hand man
a3160.name: J.D. Vance
a3160.title: US Vice-President, Donald Trump's right-hand man
a3160.speech: courageously reminded Europeans recently that Europe had become a threat to the freedom of peoples, by trying to re-enter History by breaking and entering and by deviousness, overriding the will of the peoples, notably the French and the Dutch, who had rejected the European constitutional treaty ; delivered the "Munich slap" to the European elites.

a3160.speaker: Emmanuel Todd, historian
a3160.name: Emmanuel Todd
a3160.title: historian
a3160.speech: "Europe has perhaps gone to seek its death in Ukraine" ; the Americans despise the Europeans for their servility.

a3160.speaker: Vincent Hervouet, journalist
a3160.name: Vincent Hervouet
a3160.title: journalist
a3160.speech: formulated the phrase the "half-empty word" of European diplomacy to speak of French diplomacy under Macronism.

a3395.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a3395.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.speech: Said that Tanzania expects to continue strengthening cooperation with the incoming US ambassador in various areas, such as boosting trade volume and establishing direct flights from the US to Tanzania to attract more tourists; said that further cooperation is needed in the area of technology, recognising the contribution of the US to the growth of the sector globally, that technology will enable the achievement of the government's goal of clean cooking energy and that agricultural technology will help increase production and productivity; added that it is important to continue developing cooperation in the education sector, including providing training for youths and building their capacity to create a skilled workforce that will help accelerate development.

a3395.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a3395.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.speech: Said the existing cooperation between the two countries has contributed to the progress in the health sector, including the fight against HIV/AIDS through the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), maternal and child health services and the M-Mama programme, and said Tanzania values cooperation with the US which has significantly contributed to the development of various sectors, including health and education; commended Ambassador Battle for his significant contributions during his tenure, particularly in fostering cooperation during emergencies such as the Covid-19 pandemic.

a3395.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a3395.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a3395.speech: Extended condolences following the death of the 39th US President, the late Jimmy Carter, stating that the world has lost a leader of democracy and peace, and expressed sympathy for the recent fire disaster in Los Angeles, which resulted in loss of life and property.

a3395.speaker: Michael Battle, outgoing US Ambassador to Tanzania
a3395.name: Michael Battle
a3395.title: outgoing US Ambassador to Tanzania
a3395.speech: Expressed gratitude to the government of Tanzania for the cooperation he received and assured that the incoming envoy would continue to build on the various achievements made; he noted that President Samia's "4Rs" philosophy not only represents a framework that will leave a mark on the political development reforms in the country but also serves as a testament to the world on how a nation can enact internal reforms and establish good governance aimed at effectively serving its citizens.

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Declared Prime Minister Ntsokoane Matekane "deserving of an award" for what he alleges is an unprecedented attempt to obstruct a corruption investigation into the Moshoeshoe I International Airport project ; alleges that Matekane contacted Public Accounts Committee Chairperson 'Machabana Lemphane-Letsie to interfere with the PAC's investigation into financial irregularities at the airport project, branding the move "historic" in its audacity and accusing the prime minister of undermining democratic accountability to shield allies from scrutiny ; "No prime minister in our history has directly intervened in such a blatant manner. He deserves an award for setting a disgraceful record."

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Accused the executive of plotting to even boycott the National Assembly and said the idea that the executive might sidestep parliamentary processes poses a grave threat to democracy ; "As members of the opposition, we are deeply alarmed, and so are a number of government members who still hold the nation's best interests at heart." ; "Some officials don't understand politics, nor do they comprehend administration." ; "There are only a handful of government members who truly align with the people." ; "Makhalanyane raised a critical issue and I am sure he is going to suffer political crucifixion for it." ; "These are adults, capable of making sound decisions for the good of the country. Yet, they follow one man into destruction, they lack the courage to stand up against injustice and wrongdoing."

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Claimed a yet-to-be-tabled parliamentary report contains damning revelations implicating a current cabinet minister whose two private companies were awarded contracts by the very ministry he heads, and emphasized the need for the report to be debated in parliament with its recommendations unconditionally implemented ; "The chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), 'Machabana Lemphane-Letsie, must inform the public about the contents of the report." ; "Now that he is in power, his own companies are awarded the contracts, surprisingly with inflated tender sums, one can only wonder what changed, except his position of influence."

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Drawing parallels with South Africa's Nkandla scandal involving former President Jacob Zuma, warned that Lesotho may be heading down a similar path of institutional compromise and unchecked corruption ; alleged that other MPs have been lobbying Letsie to delay the release of the report through smear tactics and covert meetings, and accused certain ministers of orchestrating a plot to undermine her integrity by circulating disrespectful messages through social media ; "Despite these efforts, she has remained steadfast. But it shows the lengths to which this government is willing to go to cover up corruption."

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Concluded with a stern warning to Matekane, urging him to be vigilant about the people surrounding him: "If he is not careful, he might find himself sharing the fate of former army commander, Tlali Kamoli, who ended up behind bars."

a3657.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3657.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3657.speech: Criticized the recent USAID funding pause as "the worst thing to happen to Lesotho."

a3657.speaker: Amnesty International (2023 report)
a3657.name: Amnesty International (2023 report)
a3657.speech: Documented impunity for police torture and killings under Matekane's watch.

a3668.speaker: Robert Benson, Center for American Progress
a3668.name: Robert Benson
a3668.title: Center for American Progress
a3668.speech: Thinks Donald Trump was already right to continue to "identify the threats posed by a revanchist Russia and an expansionist China," in the wake of outgoing president Joe Biden ; but the next occupant of the White House "is completely off the mark by alienating our allies, by pushing the Europeans to distance themselves from the United States."

a3668.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3668.name: Donald Trump
a3668.title: US President-elect
a3668.speech: In a single press conference on 7 January, threatened to annex Greenland, which is under Danish sovereignty, demanded that NATO members increase their defense budget to 5% of their GDP, declared that Canada should be the 51st American state, and warned that Washington could take back control of the Panama Canal ; had promised to end the war in Ukraine "in 24 hours," though he is no longer so assertive.

a3668.speaker: Mike Waltz, future US national security adviser
a3668.name: Mike Waltz
a3668.title: future US national security adviser
a3668.speech: Dodged the question when ABC News asked him on Sunday about the credibility of the threats uttered by his boss: "He takes very seriously the threats we face," pointing to Chinese shipping companies at the Panama Canal and Russian ships in the Arctic ; Donald Trump "will always keep all options on the table (...) unlike, it must be said, his predecessor" Joe Biden.

a3668.speaker: Mike Waltz, future US national security adviser
a3668.name: Mike Waltz
a3668.title: future US national security adviser
a3668.speech: Mentioned a continuation of aid to Kyiv to guarantee it a better position in a diplomatic negotiation, but demanded that Ukraine lower the mobilization age to "solve problems of shortages of military personnel."

a3668.speaker: Joe Biden, outgoing US President
a3668.name: Joe Biden
a3668.title: outgoing US President
a3668.speech: Praised his record on foreign policy on Monday, judging that the United States was "leading in the international competition" and would "never" be supplanted by China: "America is stronger, our alliances stronger, our adversaries and competitors weaker" ; also argued for "not abandoning" Ukraine, while his successor has threatened to cut off military support.

a3668.speaker: Joe Biden, outgoing US President
a3668.name: Joe Biden
a3668.title: outgoing US President
a3668.speech: Assured on Monday that an agreement on the war in Gaza was "on the verge" of being concluded.

a3668.speaker: European diplomats
a3668.name: European diplomats
a3668.speech: Think that there could be a form of continuity between the diplomacies of Messrs. Biden and Trump.

a3668.speaker: Lia Quartapelle, Italian member of parliament, Democratic Party
a3668.name: Lia Quartapelle
a3668.title: Italian member of parliament, Democratic Party
a3668.speech: Said she was pleasantly "surprised" by her recent visit with European parliamentarians to Washington: the American Republicans they met "had a precise idea of the interests of the United States while being open to discussion, starting with the continuation of support for Ukraine."

a3668.speaker: Jake Sullivan, US national security adviser
a3668.name: Jake Sullivan
a3668.title: US national security adviser
a3668.speech: Insisted on the "close coordination" between the outgoing Democratic administration and the incoming Republican one.

a3668.speaker: Christoph Heusgen, former representative of Germany to the UN (in Foreign Policy)
a3668.name: Christoph Heusgen
a3668.title: former representative of Germany to the UN (in Foreign Policy)
a3668.speech: Recalls a lunch in 2019 of the 15 ambassadors of the Security Council, received at the White House by a "very welcoming" Donald Trump, who listened and "devoted a lot of time to us" ; "You don't do that if you think the United Nations is useless."

a3780.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
a3780.name: Chief Sunny Onuesoke
a3780.title: Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
a3780.speech: “You do not project or rebase your economy using random databases and speculative figures. Economic rebasing must reflect real growth and measurable activities. You do not borrow to rebase — that is economic deception.”

a3780.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
a3780.name: Chief Sunny Onuesoke
a3780.title: Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
a3780.speech: Argued that Nigeria’s 2014 rebasing, which overnight made it Africa’s largest economy, was “a paper gain — one that brought prestige without progress,” and set out conditions for legitimate rebasing: it must be based on verifiable economic activities rather than donor-driven data modeling, must reflect real sector performance, “must not be funded through loans or foreign aid meant to decorate statistics,” and must be part of a broader structural reform agenda rather than an isolated PR move.

a4083.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.name: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.speech: Confirmed it has temporarily paused its foreign assistance and is re-evaluating its programs to align with President Trump's Executive Order on Re-evaluating and Realigning US Foreign Aid. "On January 20, President Trump's Executive Order on Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid paused all US foreign assistance funded by or through the State Department and USAID for review." ; "The review of all foreign assistance programs will ensure they are efficient and consistent with US foreign policy under the America First agenda." ; "The US Embassy in Zimbabwe has paused its foreign assistance and is reviewing its programs to bring them in line with this Executive Order and the waiver."

a4083.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.name: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.speech: Clarified that on January 28, Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a waiver allowing US government agencies, partners, and NGOs to continue or resume work on core life-saving initiatives, including medicine, medical services, food, shelter, subsistence assistance, and necessary administrative costs to deliver such aid.

a4083.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.name: U.S. Embassy in Zimbabwe (statement)
a4083.speech: Noted significant achievements in health, food security, and development: "The United States is proud of the gains we have helped Zimbabwe make in health, food security, and development. Today, 1.2 million Zimbabweans live longer, healthier lives because of PEPFAR's support for HIV services. More than 500 000 Zimbabweans have benefited from US humanitarian assistance during the El Nino-induced drought. Over 1 600 public hospitals and clinics have benefited from training and technical support from the United States."

a4178.speaker: Officials of the Benin Single Window Operating Company (Segub)
a4178.name: Officials of the Benin Single Window Operating Company (Segub)
a4178.speech: According to their explanations, an enormous loss of time is still observed at the port of Cotonou since it takes about fourteen days, accompanied by harassment of all kinds, to complete the administrative formalities; with the dematerialisation reform, all documents, henceforth computerised and gathered under the name of single administrative documents, should make it possible to go from fourteen to one or two working days.

a4178.speaker: Beninese authorities at the highest level
a4178.name: Beninese authorities at the highest level
a4178.speech: Acknowledged that the reform meets the fluidity needs necessary for the facilitation of Beninese trade.

a4178.speaker: Rufin Nansounon, Minister of the Maritime Economy of Benin
a4178.name: Rufin Nansounon
a4178.title: Minister of the Maritime Economy of Benin
a4178.speech: According to him, the project is placed at the centre of the government's strategies for the structural modernisation of the country, and strengthens it as a key regional actor over the long term.

a4178.speaker: Thierry Verdier, director general of Segub
a4178.name: Thierry Verdier
a4178.title: director general of Segub
a4178.speech: Said arrangements have been made to integrate the various parameters raised as concerns (the mechanism for sending documents, the legal value of dematerialised documents, the narrowness of the export network, the international legal environment) ; had also promised that his company would work in symbiosis with all the actors in order to make the system as efficient as possible.

a4178.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin
a4178.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a4178.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin
a4178.speech: Said that beyond the tools, work must be done to expand production capacity, indispensable to increasing the export margin.

a4178.speaker: Is-Dine Bouraima, director general of the Single Window for Business Formalisation (GUFE)
a4178.name: Is-Dine Bouraima
a4178.title: director general of the Single Window for Business Formalisation (GUFE)
a4178.speech: Presented the outlines of the new reform aimed at reducing the time for formalising businesses from 8 hours to one working hour ; specifies that to succeed in this reform it is imperative to settle a certain number of prerequisites, including the strengthening of the internet connection and the dematerialisation of all the related documents.

a4357.speaker: ECK Foundation, a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO)
a4357.name: ECK Foundation
a4357.title: a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO)
a4357.speech: Has warned the Federal Government that further hike in the tariff of electricity would further increase the plights of Nigerians suffered since this government came onboard less than a year ago.

a4357.speaker: Dr. Emeka Kalu, President, Eck Foundations (statement to journalists)
a4357.name: Dr. Emeka Kalu
a4357.title: President, Eck Foundations (statement to journalists)
a4357.speech: Described the hike in tariff as unguided and indiscriminatory ; insisted that this increment was bound to further impoverish the Nigerians and worsen the economic plight already plaguing the nation ; "Surreptitiously targeted at all customers under Band A who are projected to have 20-22 hours daily power supply while those under Band B to E with an estimate of 16 hours power supply would by all means frustrate the more Nigerians who have been under difficulties in the face of inflation and fuel subsidy regime change." ; "there is no justification for such hike considering that power supply generally had been at a low ebb across the federation and 95 per cent of users have not been disposed to sustain such bills." ; "This is the fourth time NERC has increased the tariff since the 2020 multi-year tariff order, but has failed to sustain power supplies in accordance with tariff charges on customers." ; explained that to critically analyse the situation, it was evident that a customer who had been purchasing 134 units monthly at N10,000 would now have to pay N40,000 naira to be able to sustain such units ; maintained that the monthly electricity subsidies promised to be reduced to 52 per cent by the regulatory commission at the tune of N131.1 billion appeared to be a mirage on the long run ; regretted that customers were being robbed their rights, while the Discos continued to abnormally exploit the citizens in the name of managing electricity power supplies ; insisted that the new tariff was being used to extort money from the public for services not consumed through electronic data system smartness ; "Discos have been perpetrating fraud since the government is unable to fact check their data, which in the end may lead Discos to surreptitiously implement the tariff hike to all electricity customers irrespective of the Band. The government is expected to urgently halt this tariff increase as its pervasive lingering effects would be greater than the negative impacts of fuel subsidy change on the nation's current economic status." ; "I therefore crave the indulgence of the government to immediately reverse such reckless increase and focus on transforming the economy whose strength has been weakened."

a4357.speaker: Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC)
a4357.name: Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC)
a4357.speech: Apologised on Wednesday to have made a mistake to charge the new tariff on all customers on equal basis, attributing such mistake to her system failure.

a4378.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) 2023 Report
a4378.name: World Food Programme (WFP) 2023 Report
a4378.speech: Revealed serious dysfunctions in the management of humanitarian aid in the Tindouf camps in Algeria, including the illegal sale of the UN agency’s products on the markets of neighbouring countries.

a4378.speaker: Promotion of Economic and Social Development (PDES), Sahrawi NGO
a4378.name: Promotion of Economic and Social Development (PDES)
a4378.title: Sahrawi NGO
a4378.speech: On Tuesday, in Geneva, alerted the international community to the alarming situation in these camps located in southwestern Algeria ; stressed the urgency of taking measures to put an end to these worrying violations, secure humanitarian corridors, and provide sustainable solutions for residents ; called on the High Commissioner for Human Rights to send a fact-finding mission to closely monitor the situation and provide transparent reports to protect the rights of those detained, in accordance with the Geneva Convention on Refugees.

a4378.speaker: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi, PDES activist
a4378.name: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi
a4378.title: PDES activist
a4378.speech: Said, during the 58th session of the Human Rights Council, that thousands of people have been living in these camps in precarious humanitarian conditions for nearly five decades, deprived of their fundamental rights, and that the security situation has also deteriorated recently, with a resurgence of criminal acts and violence, further exacerbating the suffering of the inhabitants ; added that the lack of security and stability, coupled with the lack of security and judicial mechanisms by the host country, Algeria, exposes populations to increased risks and deprives them of any form of protection or justice.

a4378.speaker: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi, PDES activist
a4378.name: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi
a4378.title: PDES activist
a4378.speech: Citing recent reports, stressed that “the geographical isolation of the camps, far from any international monitoring, contributes to the aggravation of these violations” ; specified that the most vulnerable populations, including women and children, are particularly exposed to physical and psychological violence as well as inhumane living conditions.

a4378.speaker: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi, PDES activist
a4378.name: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi
a4378.title: PDES activist
a4378.speech: “We call on the international community to redouble its efforts to ensure full respect for human rights for the populations living in the Tindouf camps,” she said ; stressed that these efforts must include the provision of unhindered humanitarian assistance, ensuring freedom of movement for residents, and establishing transparent monitoring mechanisms to track these violations and end impunity.

a4511.speaker: Russia Today website
a4511.name: Russia Today website
a4511.speech: Reported that the surprise attacks have been taking place since Russia announced the start of its operations in Ukraine, overnight into Wednesday 15 January 2025.

a4511.speaker: Russian Ministry of Defence (Telegram post)
a4511.name: Russian Ministry of Defence (Telegram post)
a4511.speech: Wrote on its Telegram account that it would retaliate forcefully for the Ukrainian attacks that targeted the area of the city of Saratov and Engels in Russia.

a4511.speaker: Russian army
a4511.name: Russian army
a4511.speech: Said that many of the missiles were neutralised by the country's air-defence system, while others that got through and hit their targets were prevented from harming civilians, particularly in areas hosting industrial infrastructure.

a4511.speaker: Ukrainian army
a4511.name: Ukrainian army
a4511.speech: Said yesterday that it is aiming to attack the regions of Bryansk, Tula and Tatarstan, areas well known for hosting chemical plants and the manufacture of weapons of war.

a4511.speaker: Russia (government)
a4511.name: Russia (government)
a4511.speech: Has been warning against the use of those weapons, claiming that their use forces it to respond by striking back with its medium-range Oreshnik missiles ; has been insisting that it is ready to go to the negotiating table only once its conditions are met by Ukraine — that Ukraine stop using US-supplied weapons to attack Russia, that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy call an election to put him in power legitimately (saying he is in office by the force of Martial Law), and that Ukraine abandon its position of seeking to join NATO.

a4511.speaker: Mark Rutte, NATO Secretary General
a4511.name: Mark Rutte
a4511.title: NATO Secretary General
a4511.speech: Speaking yesterday, said that Ukraine is not in a good position to agree to those conditions, and said that the decision would depend on the position of US President-elect Donald Trump.

a4511.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a4511.name: Donald Trump
a4511.title: US President-elect
a4511.speech: Said that once sworn into the White House he would make sure he ends the conflict within 24 hours.

a4511.speaker: Keith Kellogg, Trump appointee
a4511.name: Keith Kellogg
a4511.title: Trump appointee
a4511.speech: Claimed that the president would end the conflict within 100 days of entering office.

a4511.speaker: William Courtney, American diplomat
a4511.name: William Courtney
a4511.title: American diplomat
a4511.speech: Said that the incoming president would be able to achieve that within 100 days and not in 24 hours as he had initially promised: "I think predicting that the conflict will be ended within 24 hours is a difficult and unachievable matter, because nobody knows how the negotiations between the two sides will go." ; said that Ukraine's consecutive attacks inside Russia in recent days may send a message to Trump that the fighting can be sustained even without aid from the United States and other Western nations.

a4532.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a4532.name: Emmanuel Macron
a4532.title: President of France
a4532.speech: Said in his press conference on the situation in the Near and Middle East on 13 June 2025, concerning Israel’s massive attack on Iran: “If there is one thing that unites Israel with all its neighbours in the region, it is the Iranian threat” ; “The situation today, let us be honest and lucid, is a high-risk situation” ; “Iran has ballistic capabilities that can reach European soil.”

a4532.speaker: Élysée website (official record of the president’s statements)
a4532.name: Élysée website (official record of the president’s statements)
a4532.speech: The quotation does not appear in the summary of President Macron’s statements published below the video on the Élysée website, where it is written: “Only the spoken word is authoritative.”

a4532.speaker: A. Gotheron, press service of Médecins Sans Frontières
a4532.name: A. Gotheron
a4532.title: press service of Médecins Sans Frontières
a4532.speech: Said on 4 June 2025: “The fact that people risk dying of thirst is a very real risk.”

a4532.speaker: Organisers of the weekend demonstrations
a4532.name: Organisers of the weekend demonstrations
a4532.speech: According to organisers, several demonstrations reached at least 100,000 demonstrators calling for a ceasefire and for humanitarian aid to enter the Gaza Strip (e.g. Brussels 110,000; Paris 150,000).

a4532.speaker: CNN
a4532.name: CNN
a4532.speech: Writes that in Greece there were multiple demonstrations: in Athens, “in all the major cities of the country, but also on the islands.”

a4532.speaker: Organisers of the Hague demonstration (Amnesty International and others)
a4532.name: Organisers of the Hague demonstration (Amnesty International and others)
a4532.speech: According to the organisers, 150,000 demonstrators in The Hague on 15 June marched towards the International Court of Justice to say, among other things, no to the “genocide” in the Gaza Strip.

a4537.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4537.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4537.speech: Initially said it had to stop delivering food over concerns donations were being diverted from those in need; has now said it has decided to resume supplies in one region, saying on Tuesday that incremental supplies have begun in Tigray under a new monitoring process, first with “15kg pre-packed bags of wheat to just over 100,000 people”.

a4537.speaker: USAID
a4537.name: USAID
a4537.speech: Told journalists on Tuesday that it had no plans to resume operations, having also cut food supplies to Ethiopia around the same time as WFP.

a4566.speaker: World Bank (figures)
a4566.name: World Bank (figures)
a4566.speech: Cited as the source for the claim that more than 40% of the population lives below the extreme poverty line.

a4566.speaker: Global Terrorism Index 2024 (report)
a4566.name: Global Terrorism Index 2024 (report)
a4566.speech: According to the Global Terrorism Index 2024, Burkina Faso alone accounted for nearly half of the deaths linked to global terrorism.

a4585.speaker: Maria Zakharova, Spokeswoman for the Russian Foreign Ministry
a4585.name: Maria Zakharova
a4585.title: Spokeswoman for the Russian Foreign Ministry
a4585.speech: Denounced at her weekly briefing that "the White House's latest customs decision (...) violates the fundamental rules of the WTO, and shows that Washington does not consider itself bound by the norms of international trade law." ; Warned that the tariff war between Washington and Beijing "is all the more worrying because it concerns the world's two main economies," denouncing the "unilateral tariff protectionism" decided by Donald Trump ; "We are closely following the evolution of the situation," she continued, warning against "negative repercussions" on world markets.

a4585.speaker: China
a4585.name: China
a4585.speech: Promised a "firm and vigorous" response to the new US tariffs, including a rate of more than 100% on China.

a4585.speaker: Elvira Nabiullina, Governor of the Central Bank of Russia (BCR)
a4585.name: Elvira Nabiullina
a4585.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Russia (BCR)
a4585.speech: Indicated that the monetary institution "will take into account" this "significant new risk," while tempering that "it is still very difficult to determine where (these changes) will lead the world economy and how they will affect Russia."

a4585.speaker: Russian Finance Ministry
a4585.name: Russian Finance Ministry
a4585.speech: On Tuesday expressed concern about the "risks" of a fall in its revenues, against a backdrop of falling oil prices following the trade war launched by the United States, compounded by an OPEC announcement of a larger-than-expected increase in its production.

a4626.speaker: Somali intellectuals
a4626.name: Somali intellectuals
a4626.speech: Believe that federalism was externally imposed rather than organically developed, leading to confusion and resistance in some regions.

a4626.speaker: Allah (SWT), as quoted by the author
a4626.name: Allah (SWT)
a4626.title: as quoted by the author
a4626.speech: “He does not change a nation (for the better or worse) unless the nation changes itself from within.”

a4740.speaker: UNOPS (statement)
a4740.name: UNOPS (statement)
a4740.speech: Announced that during his visit to Ethiopia, Somalia and Sudan from 13 to 17 April, Executive Director Mr. Moreira da Silva will meet national authorities and development partners and will discuss the practical solutions that UNOPS offer to partners to maximize the impact of their humanitarian, development and peace operations — all in support of the Sustainable Development Goals; said the visit also aims at getting a better understanding of the needs on the ground, and how UNOPS can scale operations to respond.

a4740.speaker: UNOPS (statement)
a4740.name: UNOPS (statement)
a4740.speech: Said that in Sudan, where half of the population — some 25 million people — need humanitarian assistance and protection, UNOPS is strengthening health infrastructure, improving access to clean, safe water, supporting peacekeeping operations to protect civilians, and facilitating a more sustainable and equitable use of natural resources; that in Somalia, UNOPS works to strengthen the capacity of Somali institutions and supports partners in sectors such as health, governance, peace and security, and “We work to support reconstruction and state-building through disaster preparedness planning, crisis recovery, climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthening of the security sector”; and that in Ethiopia, UNOPS works with partners to support national and international development priorities, having helped strengthen health and education systems and supported food security, including environmentally friendly solutions and innovative models to modernize Ethiopia’s agriculture sector, provide clean energy to off-grid areas and improve health services across the country.

a4810.speaker: H.E Mr Prabhat Kumar, Indian High Commissioner to South Africa
a4810.name: H.E Mr Prabhat Kumar
a4810.title: Indian High Commissioner to South Africa
a4810.speech: said this was a great occasion to remember the freedom fighters and reaffirm commitment to building a stronger, self-reliant India.

a4810.speaker: H.E Mr Prabhat Kumar, Indian High Commissioner to South Africa
a4810.name: H.E Mr Prabhat Kumar
a4810.title: Indian High Commissioner to South Africa
a4810.speech: “India today is the fourth largest economy of the world. In the last 30 years we have grown from a 270 billion dollar economy to a 4 trillion dollar economy today. As we work towards celebrating India’s 100 years of independence in 2047, we aspire to grow from today’s 4 trillion dollar economy to a 30-35 trillion dollar economy. That’s the largest ever economic opportunity. Let me affirm: India is open. India is ready. We invite South Africa and other friendly nations to join us in this transformative journey together.”

a4810.speaker: Shri V Anatha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Advisor to Government of India
a4810.name: Shri V Anatha Nageswaran
a4810.title: Chief Economic Advisor to Government of India
a4810.speech: spoke to business community in South Africa on Emerging market business opportunities on 24-25 March 2025.

a4810.speaker: Patricia de Lille, South African Tourism Minister
a4810.name: Patricia de Lille
a4810.title: South African Tourism Minister
a4810.speech: announced ‘Trusted Tourist Operator Scheme’ in an effort to increase Indian tourist visitors to South Africa.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said the choice of Benin was based on a rigorous assessment of several factors, notably the quality of its application file, the dynamism of its business environment, its strategic geographical position in West Africa, and the commitment shown by the Beninese authorities to support the initiative; Benin’s willingness to promote economic cooperation within the Francophone space was also a determining factor. As for the specificity of the new model of the Economic Missions of the Francophonie (MEF), it is distinguished by strengthened collaboration between the OIF and the host country, which commits to work with the OIF on monitoring the results of the MEF, with emphasis on identifying sectors offering intra-Francophone partnership opportunities, organising qualified B2B meetings, visits to relevant economic sites, thematic workshops and reinforced support to facilitate partnerships and investments.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said the Economic Missions of the Francophonie derive from the Strategic Framework of the Francophonie 2023-2030 and the Economic Strategy for the Francophonie 2020-2025, and aim to boost trade and stimulate investment within the Francophone space by creating international growth opportunities for Francophone businesses, with particular attention to the participation of young people and women, who are the priority beneficiaries of the OIF’s cooperation projects.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said the Strategic Framework of the Francophonie 2023-2030 and the Economic Strategy for the Francophonie fall within a perspective of strengthening the OIF’s action for sustainable and inclusive development, capitalising on the richness of the French language and the diversity of Francophone cultures to generate economic opportunities — concretely, promoting entrepreneurship, supporting innovation, building the capacity of businesses, facilitating trade and investment, and networking Francophone economic actors, with the objective of making the Francophonie a space of shared, sustainable and inclusive prosperity.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said the Missions are addressed mainly to businesses from OIF member countries — SMEs, large companies, investors or bankers — wishing to develop their activities internationally, and that for each mission target economic sectors are identified according to the host country’s development potential and specific needs; for the mission in Benin, sectors such as agro-industry, cultural and creative industries coupled with sustainable tourism, and digital transformation were chosen because of their strong potential for creating wealth, added value and jobs, notably for young people and women.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said that for Beninese businesses the Economic Missions of the Francophonie represent a unique opportunity to meet potential partners from Africa, North America, Asia, Europe, the Middle East and the Indian Ocean, to explore new outlets for their products and services, to attract investment, to benefit from transfers of skills and technology, and to strengthen their international competitiveness; and that for the Beninese State, hosting this mission is an opportunity to promote the attractiveness of Benin as a destination and to showcase its economic potential and business environment to a wide audience of Francophone investors and entrepreneurs, with the arrival of delegations of about a hundred Francophone companies and economic institutions contributing concretely to the ambitious policies put in place in recent years by the government of Benin.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said the OIF has always worked in favour of development, including economic development, that a turning point came with the adoption of the Economic Strategy for the Francophonie 2020-2025, and that the establishment of these structured and regular Economic Missions responds to its wish to innovate, transform its actions in the economic field and make them more visible; the enthusiasm created by the Economic Missions and the growing number of company registrations from mission to mission show that the OIF is on the right track with this flagship economic project.

a4822.speaker: Thi Hoang Mai Tran, OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.name: Thi Hoang Mai Tran
a4822.title: OIF Representative for West Africa
a4822.speech: Said, responding to criticism of the OIF’s strong political character, that the OIF has a holistic mission embracing the promotion of the French language, cultural diversity, education, democracy and peace, as well as sustainable development; that economic action has always been an essential component of that mission because economic prosperity is a fundamental pillar of development and stability; and that initiatives like the Economic Missions of the Francophonie are part of this global vision — demonstrating that “the Francophonie is a living force at the service of the socio-economic development of its member States and governments.”

a4861.speaker: Sintiki Tafra-Ube, Director of Humanitarian and Social Affairs of the ECOWAS Commission
a4861.name: Sintiki Tafra-Ube
a4861.title: Director of Humanitarian and Social Affairs of the ECOWAS Commission
a4861.speech: Said the humanitarian assistance was to complement the efforts of the government of Cabo Verde in alleviating the suffering of the vulnerable in the wake of the floods: "We are delighted that Cape Verde is one of the countries to benefit, with an allocation of 770,143 dollars to support vulnerable populations in the country."

a4861.speaker: Lidia Lida, Secretary of State for Social Inclusion of Cabo Verde
a4861.name: Lidia Lida
a4861.title: Secretary of State for Social Inclusion of Cabo Verde
a4861.speech: Expressed appreciation to the ECOWAS Commission, noting that the humanitarian support would go a long way in helping the vulnerable get back on their feet: "We have been implementing the strategy to eradicate extreme poverty with Cape Verde's own resources within the scope of the state budget, but also with the combined efforts of Cape Verde and its international partners, and it is in this sense that the financial support from ECOWAS has complemented our actions within the scope of this strategy to eradicate extreme poverty."

a5060.speaker: Admiral Abdi Warsame, Commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defense, and Admiral Karambir Singh, Chief of the Naval Staff of India
a5060.name: Admiral Abdi Warsame
a5060.title: Commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defense, and Admiral Karambir Singh, Chief of the Naval Staff of India
a5060.speech: Discussed the bilateral relations and cooperation between the Somali Navy and the Indian Navy, and the two naval chiefs agreed to strengthen their collaboration in areas such as anti-piracy operations, maritime domain awareness, capacity building, and training.

a5282.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO), Health Emergency Appeal 2025
a5282.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5282.title: Health Emergency Appeal 2025
a5282.speech: Is launching an appeal for 1.5 billion US dollars as part of its Health Emergency Appeal 2025 to support life-saving health interventions worldwide; the appeal sets out the main priorities and essential resources needed to respond to 42 ongoing health emergencies, including 17 grade 3 crises, and highlights four major challenges: climate change, conflicts, population displacement and epidemics. WHO said it is committed to providing emergency health assistance, notably in conflict zones such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the occupied Palestinian territory and Sudan, and intends to fulfil its unique role while respecting the principles of international humanitarian law, ensuring that no one is left behind.

a5282.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a5282.name: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a5282.title: WHO Director-General
a5282.speech: "Conflicts, disease outbreaks, climate-related disasters and other health emergencies are no longer isolated or occasional situations - they are relentless, overlapping and intensifying." ; "Whether it is fighting cholera outbreaks or providing mental health support in conflict zones, WHO's action extends beyond the immediate care we provide. We give communities the means to protect themselves, to prioritise equity and to build a legacy of preparedness. This appeal aims to enable WHO to save lives, to protect the right to health and to give hope where there is none."

a5663.speaker: S&P Global, international financial analytics corporation
a5663.name: S&P Global
a5663.title: international financial analytics corporation
a5663.speech: Has described the 650,000 barrels per day Dangote Oil Refinery and Petrochemicals company as capable of resolving Nigeria's foreign exchange issue and its huge pressure on the local Naira currency, while also catalysing the country's economic development; noted that the largest single-train refinery complex in the world would bolster Nigeria's oil sector and, more importantly, also have a positive impact on its growing economy.

a5663.speaker: Ravi Bhatia, Director and Lead Analyst, Sovereign and International Public Finance Ratings, S&P Global Ratings
a5663.name: Ravi Bhatia
a5663.title: Director and Lead Analyst, Sovereign and International Public Finance Ratings, S&P Global Ratings
a5663.speech: Said Dangote refinery would transform Nigeria into a net exporter of petroleum products, and added that this transformation is expected to boost revenue generation and alleviate the current pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves: “It is a very impressive facility, able to process 650,000 barrels a day, when in full capacity. It is the largest single-train refinery complex in the world. It came out quite quickly. Nigeria is a big exporter of crude but has issues with importing refined fuels. So, there is a gap in the market where crude can be refined in Nigeria, save money that way, and potentially save some foreign exchange. This will be positive for the economy in the medium term. It looks positive from our assessment.”

a5663.speaker: Devakumar Edwin, Vice President of Oil and Gas at Dangote Industries Limited (DIL)
a5663.name: Devakumar Edwin
a5663.title: Vice President of Oil and Gas at Dangote Industries Limited (DIL)
a5663.speech: Reiterated that by harnessing Africa's abundant crude oil resources to produce refined products locally, the company aims to catalyse a virtuous cycle of industrial development, job creation, and economic prosperity; revealed that, as earlier promised, the company will start the production of premium motor spirit (PMS) this month (July); noting that products from the $20 billion facility are of high quality and meet international standards, said it can meet 100 per cent of Nigeria's demand for petrol, diesel, kerosene, and aviation Jet, with surpluses available for export; said the refinery, currently operating at 350,000 barrels per day, is slated to scale up to at least 500,000 barrels per day by July/August; noted the refinery conforms to Euro V specifications and is designed to comply with US EPA, EU emission norms, DPR emission/effluent norms and ARDA standards; and said it is a thing of pride that a Nigerian company designed and built the world's largest single-train refinery complex while acting directly as its own EPC contractor.

a5663.speaker: The S&P team
a5663.name: The S&P team
a5663.speech: Commended the President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, for integrating advanced technologies and quality control measures, including a state-of-the-art Central Control Unit ensuring smooth automation of operations.

a5731.speaker: Michael Chertoff
a5731.name: Michael Chertoff
a5731.speech: “We always monitor the flow of information, intelligence, threat streams to see whether we have any indication there’s some imminent. We work hard to identify potential cells and disrupt them. This is one of the reasons we put so much emphasis on intelligence gathering.”

a5731.speaker: People of the Zike community, Plateau State (cited in a HumanAngle report)
a5731.name: People of the Zike community
a5731.title: Plateau State (cited in a HumanAngle report)
a5731.speech: Opined that “the attack could have been prevented, as they received warnings of an impending attack and notified security.”

a5731.speaker: HumanAngle (report)
a5731.name: HumanAngle (report)
a5731.speech: Cited “limited firepower, the rough terrain of the area, and the fact that Zike had never been attacked before as the cause of the inaction.”

a5731.speaker: Thomas Fingar, former Chairman of the US National Intelligence Council and Deputy Director of National Intelligence for Analysis, in his book “Reducing Uncertainty”
a5731.name: Thomas Fingar
a5731.title: former Chairman of the US National Intelligence Council and Deputy Director of National Intelligence for Analysis, in his book “Reducing Uncertainty”
a5731.speech: Summarised that the US government spends billions of dollars every year for the Intelligence Community to reduce uncertainties.

a5774.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.speech: Launched an urgent appeal on Thursday in the face of the worsening violence in El Fasher and its surroundings, in North Darfur; in a report entitled “Besieged, attacked, starved,” MSF denounces mass abuses: massacres, looting, sexual violence, abductions and famine; the NGO calls for an immediate halt to the violence, in particular ethnically targeted attacks, and demands unimpeded humanitarian access.

a5774.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.speech: Declared: “We are deeply worried by the threat of a large-scale offensive against the hundreds of thousands of inhabitants of El Fasher,” underlining the gravity of the daily fighting in the city.

a5774.speaker: MSF report “Besieged, attacked, starved” (based on more than 80 interviews conducted between May 2024 and May 2025 with patients and displaced people)
a5774.name: MSF report “Besieged
a5774.title: attacked, starved” (based on more than 80 interviews conducted between May 2024 and May 2025 with patients and displaced people)
a5774.speech: Documents systematic violence, notably by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their allies; testimonies report deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and explicit threats to “cleanse” El Fasher by the RSF; the report also denounces indiscriminate air strikes by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), responsible for extensive damage in civilian areas.

a5774.speaker: Michel-Olivier Lacharité, head of emergencies at MSF
a5774.name: Michel-Olivier Lacharité
a5774.title: head of emergencies at MSF
a5774.speech: Said that civilians are being targeted because of their ethnic affiliation.

a5774.speaker: Mathilde Simon, humanitarian affairs adviser (MSF)
a5774.name: Mathilde Simon
a5774.title: humanitarian affairs adviser (MSF)
a5774.speech: Warned: “We fear a scenario similar to El Fasher. This spiral of violence must be stopped.”

a5774.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5774.speech: Recalls that this violence comes two years after the ethnically motivated massacre of the Masalit community in West Darfur in June 2023; MSF-supported health facilities have suffered at least seven attacks, forcing the organisation to suspend its activities in El Fasher in August 2024 and then in Zamzam in February 2025.

a5774.speaker: A female resident of El Fasher (witness)
a5774.name: A female resident of El Fasher (witness)
a5774.speech: Testifies: “The planes bombed our neighbourhood, then the pilots came to apologise. There was no RSF presence.”

a5794.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Turkey
a5794.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
a5794.title: President of Turkey
a5794.speech: Says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is the “biggest obstacle to regional peace” and that Israeli attacks on Iran right before a new round of nuclear talks with the United States aimed to sabotage the negotiations; urged countries with influence over Israel not to listen to its “poison” and to seek a solution to the fighting via dialogue without allowing a wider conflict. “Netanyahu’s Zionist ambitions have no other purpose than to drag our region and … the whole world into a big disaster,” he added. ; Accused the Western leaders of providing “unconditional support” to Israel and said Turkiye would not allow borders in the Middle East to be redrawn “in blood”. ; “It is vital for us to show more solidarity to end Israel’s banditry – not only in Palestine but also in Syria, in Lebanon and in Iran,” he told the OIC gathering.

a5794.speaker: Hakan Fidan, Turkish Foreign Minister
a5794.name: Hakan Fidan
a5794.title: Turkish Foreign Minister
a5794.speech: Accused Israel of leading the Middle East towards “total disaster” by attacking Iran. “Israel is now leading the region to the brink of total disaster by attacking Iran, our neighbour,” he said. “There is no Palestinian, Lebanese, Syrian, Yemeni or Iranian problem but there is clearly an Israeli problem.”

a5794.speaker: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5794.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5794.speech: The 57-member OIC, founded in 1969, says its mission is to “safeguard and protect the interests of the Muslim world in the spirit of promoting international peace and harmony”.

a5794.speaker: Sinem Koseoglu, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Istanbul
a5794.name: Sinem Koseoglu
a5794.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Istanbul
a5794.speech: Said Turkiye as the current OIC chair sees itself well-placed in helping to find a resolution to the Israel-Iran conflict. “It is a NATO member country placed between the Western and Muslim worlds, and has strong bilateral relations with Iran, the Western world and the United States. And until a few years ago, it had strong relations with Israel,” she said.

a5794.speaker: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister
a5794.name: Abbas Araghchi
a5794.title: Iranian Foreign Minister
a5794.speech: Said his country was only prepared to engage with the US if Israel stops its attacks on Iran. “Iran is ready to consider diplomacy once again and once the aggression is stopped and the aggressor is held accountable for the crimes committed,” said Araghchi. “We support the continuation of discussion with [Britain, France, Germany and the EU] and express our readiness to meet again in the near future.”

a5955.speaker: Coalitions of “Francophone” Africa for the International Criminal Court (CAF-CPI), declaration of 30 April 2024
a5955.name: Coalitions of “Francophone” Africa for the International Criminal Court (CAF-CPI)
a5955.title: declaration of 30 April 2024
a5955.speech: Asserted that the situation in Burkina Faso constitutes cases of “human rights violations”; affirmed that the country has been grappling with an Islamist insurgency since 2016; equated the VDP with a militia; designated the perpetrators of abuses, among whom they cite the Burkinabe armed forces and the VDP, on the same footing as the “insurgent Islamists”; and recommended that judicial proceedings be initiated against the perpetrators of these abuses and that the ICC conduct investigations to elucidate the case.

a5955.speaker: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations, right of reply)
a5955.name: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations
a5955.title: right of reply)
a5955.speech: React to the CAF-CPI declaration, noting that no Burkinabe human rights organisation signed it and that the coalition’s “colonial Francophone identity is palpable proof that it cannot credibly carry the voice of Africa”; argue that its renewed activism could be intrinsically linked to threats to the interests of the former French metropole in the Sahel States; recall that the United States is not a signatory to the Rome Statute and so is not subject to ICC jurisdiction; state that investigations have been opened at national level into the alleged violations by the Burkinabe armed forces and the VDP; and say Human Rights Watch “cannot be a judicial body and has no competence in matters of judicial policing.”

a5955.speaker: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations, right of reply)
a5955.name: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations
a5955.title: right of reply)
a5955.speech: On the nature of the conflict and the VDP: say Burkina Faso faces “an asymmetric war that has been imposed upon it” rather than an Islamist insurgency, and that the population has witnessed killings of Muslims in mosques and even during Ramadan; state that the VDP receive training in international humanitarian law before deployment and are supervised by the regular army, that recruitment does not target particular ethnic groups, and that allegations of ethnic targeting are “mendacious and slanderous” propaganda that “denotes a desire to create fertile ground for a civil war in our country.”

a5955.speaker: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations, right of reply)
a5955.name: Coordination of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders (civil society organisations
a5955.title: right of reply)
a5955.speech: Recommendations and declaration: while subscribing to the call for judicial proceedings, encourage the “world’s policemen” and the “Don Quixotes” of human rights to cease feeding terrorism through passive and active complicity, cease financing terrorism through ransom payments, end the instrumentalisation of terrorism for geopolitical and geostrategic ambitions, and support without hypocrisy the States fighting terrorism; announce the creation of the Citizens’ Coalition of Pan-Africanist Organisations and Leaders Engaged for the Sovereignty of Africa and the Defence of Pan-African Leaders (CoCiPESAD); and reaffirm “unconditional support for the authorities of the Transition, headed by comrade Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of the Transition, Head of State. The Homeland or Death, We Shall Overcome!”

a5972.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5972.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5972.title: President of Ghana
a5972.speech: Directed his finance minister, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, to take immediate steps to address the significant funding gap caused by the suspension of USAID's international funding programme ; expressed deep concern over the potential impact of the funding gap ; emphasised that the suspension of USAID funding could severely affect the availability of antiretroviral drugs, HIV testing, and prevention programmes, as well as other critical health interventions ; instructed the finance minister to prioritise bridging arrangements for these key areas to ensure continuity in service delivery and safeguard public health outcomes.

a5972.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Spokesperson to the President and Minister for Government Communications (statement)
a5972.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a5972.title: Spokesperson to the President and Minister for Government Communications (statement)
a5972.speech: "The President is deeply committed to protecting the gains made in these critical sectors and has directed that urgent steps be taken to address the funding gap," the statement read.

a5990.speaker: Emelia Mahama, Women Economic Empowerment Technical Specialist for PROSPER III
a5990.name: Emelia Mahama
a5990.title: Women Economic Empowerment Technical Specialist for PROSPER III
a5990.speech: Lauded the women’s achievements and emphasised the importance of empowering women in agriculture ; “This is a testament to the need to build more resilient communities through sustainable farming practices and stronger financial independence for women,” she stated, crediting these gains to collaborative efforts with local and national stakeholders.

a5990.speaker: Dorcas Osei, farmer and leader from Bayerebon No. 3
a5990.name: Dorcas Osei
a5990.title: farmer and leader from Bayerebon No. 3
a5990.speech: Expressed gratitude for CARE’s training and support, noting how the project has transformed her livelihood and empowered women to make meaningful contributions to their communities ; “This project has not only transformed my livelihood but has empowered many women here to make meaningful contributions to our families and communities” ; “This recognition encourages us as women to continue to work hard to make farming profitable and attractive, especially for other women.”

a5990.speaker: Mr Farouk, Atwima Mponua District Agricultural Director
a5990.name: Mr Farouk
a5990.title: Atwima Mponua District Agricultural Director
a5990.speech: Praised the awardees and commended CARE International’s support, emphasising that the initiative not only uplifts individual women but also strengthens entire communities ; “The awards amplify our appreciation of our farmers while demonstrating our commitment to a robust agricultural community.”

a6002.speaker: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates, and Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle, Chairman of the Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
a6002.name: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi
a6002.title: Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates, and Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle, Chairman of the Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
a6002.speech: The two leaders agreed that emergency aid should be delivered to the affected areas before the beginning of Ramadan, and also agreed that important dams should be repaired to reduce the risk of floods caused by the spring rains, which are expected to start in April.

a6002.speaker: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates
a6002.name: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi
a6002.title: Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates
a6002.speech: Updated the chairman on the progress of the UAE-funded wells project, which aims to provide clean water to the communities in need; said that the first phase of the project, which involved drilling 100 wells, has been completed and the second phase, which will drill another 100 wells, is underway.

a6002.speaker: Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle, Chairman of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6002.name: Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle
a6002.title: Chairman of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6002.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the UAE government for its unwavering support with the Somali government and the Somali people; said that the UAE is a true friend and partner of Somalia, and that the cooperation between the two countries will enhance the resilience and development of Somalia.

a6002.speaker: Joint statement by the UAE ambassador and the SoDMA chairman
a6002.name: Joint statement by the UAE ambassador and the SoDMA chairman
a6002.speech: The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the bilateral relations and cooperation between the UAE and Somalia, especially in the areas of humanitarian assistance, disaster management, and resilience projects.

a6126.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) (report received by APA)
a6126.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) (report received by APA)
a6126.speech: Reveals a worrying deterioration in the situation of women and girls in conflict zones in Mali: according to its May 2025 survey, the number of internally displaced persons has almost reached 380,000, up from 330,000 in May 2024, a rise of nearly 15%, accompanied by a resurgence of sexual violence in displacement sites and conflict zones; documents cases of “sexual exploitation, harassment and forced marriage” amid persistent instability particularly affecting the Timbuktu, Gao, Mopti and Ménaka regions.

a6126.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a6126.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a6126.speech: Stresses that “women and girls are at the heart of these vulnerabilities and are disproportionately affected by this insecurity and the humanitarian crisis”; states that fewer than a quarter of health facilities in affected regions provide comprehensive care or support for survivors of sexual violence and that nearly half of specialised services remain closed nationwide.

a6126.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a6126.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a6126.speech: Says it is maintaining its operations, supporting 86 health facilities, six safe spaces for women and girls, and seven one-stop centres in the worst-affected regions, and that in May its mobile teams provided services to nearly 3,000 people in displacement camps, 80% of them women and girls; warns that of the $16.5 million appeal for 2025 it has received only $2.9 million, leaving a “colossal shortfall of $13.5 million”, and that “without urgent additional funding” the scale and sustainability of programmes against sexual violence and reproductive health services are threatened, while nearly 900,000 women and girls are targeted by these interventions.

a6374.speaker: Energy Regulation Board (ERB)
a6374.name: Energy Regulation Board (ERB)
a6374.speech: Says it has put in place measures to ensure that there is no disruption in the fuel supply chain following a strike by transporters in Mozambique.

a6374.speaker: Namukolo Kasumpa, Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.name: Namukolo Kasumpa
a6374.title: Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.speech: Said the strike in Mozambique was likely to exacerbate the ongoing logistical challenges being experienced by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) in transporting petroleum products into the country by road. "The Government of the Republic of Zambia is aware of this development and is closely monitoring the situation through the Mission in Mozambique to ascertain and determine the extent of the impact this will have on the importation of petroleum products from the Port of Beira in Mozambique." ; "The ERB is actively monitoring the situation in Mozambique; The ERB is encouraging OMCs to consider using other import routes like the port of Dar es salaam in Tanzania during this period of the strike in Mozambique."

a6374.speaker: Namukolo Kasumpa, Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.name: Namukolo Kasumpa
a6374.title: Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.speech: Said the ERB was working with relevant government ministries and agencies to mitigate any fuel supply challenges that might arise going forward and ensure a consistent and reliable fuel supply; explained that ERB had engaged OMCs and urged them to use the pre-clearance facility provided for importation of petroleum products by the Zambia Revenue Authority to reduce the time that fuel tankers spent at Chanida border, and that it had also extended driving hours for tankers from the recommended 06:00 to 18:00 hours to 05:00 to 22:00 hours.

a6374.speaker: Namukolo Kasumpa, Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.name: Namukolo Kasumpa
a6374.title: Energy Regulation Board (ERB) public relations manager
a6374.speech: "The ERB wishes to reassure the public that there is sufficient stock to cover the national requirements of petroleum products. As of 5th November 2024, the country has 28.558, 416.80 million litters of diesel and 14, 057, 078.70 million liters of petrol in various depots and retail sites countrywide."

a6374.speaker: Mozambique (government announcement)
a6374.name: Mozambique (government announcement)
a6374.speech: Announced a scheduled strike by the Mozambican Federation of Road Transport Association to take place from November 1 to 7, 2024.

a6382.speaker: Alex Majogoro, Acting Director of the Nelico organisation (reading the annual NGO report for Geita region)
a6382.name: Alex Majogoro
a6382.title: Acting Director of the Nelico organisation (reading the annual NGO report for Geita region)
a6382.speech: Said that as a result of the decision by US President Donald Trump to suspend 90 percent of funding through USAID, many organisations have been left shaken. "Apart from the suspension of the PEPFAR programme, other projects that have been suspended include campaigns against malaria as well as basic health services" ; said many organisations depend on funding from international donors, so the absence of those funds has caused a decline in health services, the halting of some development projects and a large gap in the areas that had depended on that assistance.

a6382.speaker: Alex Majogoro, Acting Director of the Nelico organisation
a6382.name: Alex Majogoro
a6382.title: Acting Director of the Nelico organisation
a6382.speech: Said some organisations in the region have been forced to cut staff by more than 50 percent, while others have had to cut employees' salaries in order to cope with the challenge of dependence on donor funding; another challenge is the difficulty of obtaining tax exemptions, despite many organisations having applied to be recognised as charitable institutions.

a6382.speaker: NaCONGO
a6382.name: NaCONGO
a6382.speech: According to NaCONGO, many organisations, especially the younger ones, have failed to carry out their responsibilities, while others have closed their offices for lack of funding.

a6382.speaker: Paulina Alex, chairperson of NaCONGO in Geita region
a6382.name: Paulina Alex
a6382.title: chairperson of NaCONGO in Geita region
a6382.speech: Said that alongside those challenges, non-governmental organisations have nevertheless succeeded in implementing various interventions, including child protection and human rights, the fight against harmful traditional practices and child marriage, the fight against drugs, health, education, the environment and the provision of legal aid; said more than 50 projects have been implemented in Geita region and more than 300 groups of women and young people have been economically empowered through loans. "Through these organisations, more than 10 health centres have been renovated and equipped. Some 480 citizens have been given legal aid, but also in the employment sector, these 70 organisations that are here in our region have provided jobs for 500 people."

a6382.speaker: Regional NGO statistics (Geita)
a6382.name: Regional NGO statistics (Geita)
a6382.speech: Statistics show that non-governmental organisations invested 7.2 billion shillings in 2024/25 in the health, education, agriculture, social welfare and environment sectors and in the fight against gender-based violence.

a6382.speaker: Deodatus Kayango, Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a6382.name: Deodatus Kayango
a6382.title: Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a6382.speech: Opening the meeting, stressed the importance of cooperation between the Government and the organisations, saying, "The Government recognises the great work being done by NGOs in bringing development to citizens" ; said the aim of the meeting was to meet with all the non-governmental organisations in order to discuss various issues for improving services and strengthening cooperation in implementing projects and social services.

a6382.speaker: Deodatus Kayango, Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a6382.name: Deodatus Kayango
a6382.title: Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a6382.speech: Speaking about the general election expected in October this year, asked the organisations authorised to provide civic education to bear patriotism in mind. "We are heading towards an election. Non-governmental organisations that have received authorisation to provide education, provide civic education with patriotism in mind. If civic education is provided well, the community will gain a good awareness and will turn out to elect good leaders."

a6437.speaker: Brigade Kher Thon, Ulang County Relief and Rehabilitation coordinator
a6437.name: Brigade Kher Thon
a6437.title: Ulang County Relief and Rehabilitation coordinator
a6437.speech: "Since last year, some villages and farms have been submerged by water, most of the population were displaced from their homes and are in dire need of humanitarian assistance, including food, shelter and medical supplies."

a6437.speaker: Mary Kong, 50-year-old resident of Ulang County
a6437.name: Mary Kong
a6437.title: 50-year-old resident of Ulang County
a6437.speech: Explained the problems encountered by local families and urged the peacekeepers to share their concerns with relevant stakeholders: "We face so many challenges, including a lack of food and clean drinking water. We have to fetch water directly from the river, which sometimes causes illness among our children. There are also inadequate medical facilities." ; "We beg you to raise these issues with the State authorities and humanitarian organizations so that they can support us with life-saving assistance."

a6437.speaker: Lieutenant Anisa Mukashema, UNMISS female engagement team commander, from Rwanda
a6437.name: Lieutenant Anisa Mukashema
a6437.title: UNMISS female engagement team commander, from Rwanda
a6437.speech: Stressed the mission's commitment to working closely with all partners to improve security: "We engage with women in the community so that they share their experiences and challenges." ; "We cannot always solve the many issues they face, but we amplify their voices and advocate for their rights and safety as well as engaging in a broader effort to foster inclusive and lasting peace."

a6514.speaker: Sebastian !Gobs, Constituency Councillor (Khorixas)
a6514.name: Sebastian !Gobs
a6514.title: Constituency Councillor (Khorixas)
a6514.speech: Confirmed in an interview with nbc News that, as drought persists across the Kunene Region, Khorixas' constituency office is challenged by transport to deliver much-needed food aid to rural residents.

a6514.speaker: A caretaker for displaced people at the Katutura Youth Complex
a6514.name: A caretaker for displaced people at the Katutura Youth Complex
a6514.speech: Has appealed to good Samaritans, including the government, to come to the aid of the homeless.

a6729.speaker: U.S. Department of State (report distributed by the APO Group)
a6729.name: U.S. Department of State (report distributed by the APO Group)
