a6729.speech: Stated that in Berlin Assistant Secretary Witkowsky will lead an interagency delegation to the second U.S.–Germany Conflict Prevention and Stabilization Dialogue hosted by Germany's Director-General for Crisis Prevention, Stabilization, Peacebuilding, and Humanitarian Assistance, where they will discuss areas of shared interest and cooperation including activities under the U.S. Strategy to Prevent Conflict and Promote Stability; that she will take part in the third plenary of the Berlin Climate Security Conference and in a joint roundtable with Director-General Potzel co-hosted by U.S. Embassy Berlin and the German Council on Foreign Relations focused on women, peace, and security; that the delegation will travel to northern Ghana to launch the Coastal States Stability Mechanism (CSSM), co-developed by USAID and Germany, and will discuss CSSM initiatives to expand and improve government delivery of critical services and support efforts to promote social and economic resilience in the face of instability and conflict; that they will meet with local government officials, traditional leaders, and civil society representatives; and that in Accra the delegation will meet with Ghanaian officials to discuss shared priorities for countering violent extremism and enhancing cooperation through the Strategy to Prevent Conflict and Promote Stability.

a6729.speaker: Assistant Secretary Witkowsky, U.S. Department of State
a6729.name: Assistant Secretary Witkowsky
a6729.title: U.S. Department of State
a6729.speech: Will underscore the growing intersection of conflict prevention and climate-related efforts, advocating for integrated approaches as outlined in the newly released U.S. Framework for Climate Resilience and Security.

a6902.speaker: Two senior EU officials (anonymous)
a6902.name: Two senior EU officials (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Told Reuters on Monday that the European Union executive has temporarily suspended funding for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Somalia, after a UN investigation found widespread theft and misuse of aid meant to avert famine.

a6902.speaker: UN data
a6902.name: UN data
a6902.speech: The European Commission gave more than $7 million in aid to the WFP's operations in Somalia last year, a fraction of the donations of more than $1 billion it received, UN data shows.

a6902.speaker: Balazs Ujvari, spokesman for the European Commission
a6902.name: Balazs Ujvari
a6902.title: spokesman for the European Commission
a6902.speech: Neither confirmed nor denied specifically a temporary suspension but said: “So far, the EU has not been informed by its UN partners of a financial impact on EU-funded projects. Nevertheless, we will continue to monitor the situation and abide by our zero-tolerance approach to fraud, corruption or misconduct.”

a6902.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6902.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6902.speech: The WFP did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

a6902.speaker: One senior EU official (anonymous)
a6902.name: One senior EU official (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Said the decision was taken after the UN investigation concluded that landowners, local authorities, members of the security forces and humanitarian workers were all involved in stealing aid intended for vulnerable people ; Said the aid would be restored after the WFP met additional conditions, such as vetting of partners on the ground in Somalia ; Said the European Commission contributes €10 million to Somalia and Ethiopia via the WFP, with the suspension covering part of that.

a6902.speaker: Second senior EU official (anonymous)
a6902.name: Second senior EU official (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Confirmed that the aid would be restored after the WFP met additional conditions, such as vetting of partners on the ground in Somalia.

a6902.speaker: A third source, also an EU official (anonymous)
a6902.name: A third source
a6902.title: also an EU official (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Said the Commission was “cooperating actively with WFP to resolve systemic defects” but said no aid was suspended at this stage.

a6902.speaker: UN report of 7 July (marked “strictly confidential”), commissioned by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a6902.name: UN report of 7 July (marked “strictly confidential”)
a6902.title: commissioned by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a6902.speech: It cited internally displaced persons (IDPs) as saying they were coerced into paying up to half of the cash assistance they received to people in positions of power in the face of threats of eviction, arrest or de-registration from beneficiary lists ; The UN report did not attempt to quantify the amount of aid diverted but said its findings “suggest that post-delivery aid diversion in Somalia is widespread and systemic” ; Investigators found aid diversion at all of the 55 IDP sites in Somalia from which they collected data, the report said ; It identified a variety of perpetrators, led by so-called “gatekeepers,” powerful individuals from dominant local clans; these gatekeepers leverage their influence over access to camp sites and food beneficiary lists to coerce payments from IDPs, the report said; members of security forces also play a role by intimidating and sometimes arresting those who refuse to pay, while some humanitarian workers collude with gatekeepers to pocket stolen funds, the report said ; While famine has been averted for now, the report warned that inadequate humanitarian funding could imperil fragile progress.

a6902.speaker: Devex
a6902.name: Devex
a6902.speech: Its contents were first published on Monday by Devex, a media outlet focused on international development.

a6902.speaker: Jessica Jennings, USAID spokesperson
a6902.name: Jessica Jennings
a6902.title: USAID spokesperson
a6902.speech: Said in a statement the United States was working to understand the extent of the diversion and was “already taking steps to protect beneficiaries and ensure taxpayer money is used to benefit vulnerable persons in Somalia, as intended.”

a6902.speaker: An official of USAID (anonymous)
a6902.name: An official of USAID (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Said the situations in Ethiopia and Somalia were different and USAID was not planning to pause food assistance in the latter.

a6902.speaker: A US Congressional source (anonymous)
a6902.name: A US Congressional source (anonymous)
a6902.speech: Said the decision to suspend aid in Ethiopia was, in part, related to the uniquely hands-on role of the federal government there in distributing food assistance, which has long made donors uneasy ; “The widespread theft of food assistance in Ethiopia was abhorrent, but was also an opportunity to change the way it is provided.”

a6902.speaker: Somali Disaster Management Office (statement)
a6902.name: Somali Disaster Management Office (statement)
a6902.speech: Said in a statement on Monday that Somali authorities were committed to investigating the U.N. report's findings, while adding that current aid delivery systems operate “outside of the government channels”.

a6902.speaker: Office of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a6902.name: Office of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a6902.speech: Guterres' office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

a6902.speaker: Humanitarian officials
a6902.name: Humanitarian officials
a6902.speech: Warned of a looming famine due to the Horn of Africa's worst drought in decades.

a6902.speaker: Official data / researchers
a6902.name: Official data / researchers
a6902.speech: Famine was averted, official data shows, but as many as 43 000 people, half of them children younger than five, died last year as a result of the drought, researchers estimate.

a6902.speaker: United Nations
a6902.name: United Nations
a6902.speech: Aid budgets are under strain globally, with just 36% funded to date of the $2.6 billion the UN says is needed this year for Somalia's humanitarian response.

a7070.speaker: Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (Mera)
a7070.name: Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (Mera)
a7070.speech: Said yesterday that fuel importation is partly being hampered by lack of foreign exchange, while not being clear on stock levels, apart from assuring that the situation will improve within this week.

a7070.speaker: Mera, National Oil Company of Malawi (Nocma) and the Ministry of Energy
a7070.name: Mera
a7070.title: National Oil Company of Malawi (Nocma) and the Ministry of Energy
a7070.speech: Gave an assurance last month that about 160 million litres of fuel were procured to cover September and October.

a7070.speaker: Frank Banda, Transporters Association of Malawi (TAM) spokesperson
a7070.name: Frank Banda
a7070.title: Transporters Association of Malawi (TAM) spokesperson
a7070.speech: Said about 125 trucks carrying petrol and diesel are stuck in Dar es Salaam, waiting for clearance from the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) which requires that fuel suppliers pay tax, but also other travel documents and ensuring that there are tracking gadgets on all vehicles: "There are 25 trucks already loaded with petrol, but have not been cleared by the TRA. We hope that they will be cleared today [Monday]. We also sent 100 more trucks, whose loading has not been done and these are just waiting because of low stocks."

a7070.speaker: A source in the private sector (anonymous)
a7070.name: A source in the private sector (anonymous)
a7070.speech: Corroborated the situation, saying there is very little fuel available: "The authorities are banking on Beira in Mozambique where there is 10 million litres of diesel and petrol, but the challenge is that at Beira, loading is on priority basis. So we have trucks from Zambia and Tanzania being loaded."

a7070.speaker: Raymond Likambale, Nocma spokesperson
a7070.name: Raymond Likambale
a7070.title: Nocma spokesperson
a7070.speech: Could not be reached for comment yesterday.

a7070.speaker: Fitina Khonje, Mera spokesperson
a7070.name: Fitina Khonje
a7070.title: Mera spokesperson
a7070.speech: Admitted that the nation is facing importation challenges, saying in a written response: "The country is experiencing fuel supply challenges. However, the country is expecting some more inflows within the week. This is still a forex-induced challenge. However, arrangements under G2G and other supply contracts are still in place."

a7070.speaker: Henry Kachaje, Mera chief executive officer
a7070.name: Henry Kachaje
a7070.title: Mera chief executive officer
a7070.speech: Said during a press briefing in Lilongwe on August 29 that fuel on open tender system (OTS) was already flowing into the country: "The country will in a few weeks be receiving a G2G vessel bringing a total of 48 million litres of both petrol and diesel. Additionally, 56 million litres of petrol and 57 million litres of diesel have been secured from OTS suppliers, in total bringing an expected volume of over 160 million litres."

a7070.speaker: Nocma data
a7070.name: Nocma data
a7070.speech: Shows that Malawi uses one million litres for petrol and 850,000 litres of diesel on a daily basis, translating to a combined 55.5 million litres a month.

a7070.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a7070.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a7070.speech: According to the Bank, Malawi spends $600 million (about K1 trillion) on fuel importation per year; in total, the country needs $3 billion to meet its import requirements against export earnings of $1 billion.

a7078.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.name: Boni Yayi
a7078.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.speech: Commented: “This is a mark of love and friendship, in that the amount of the second compact exceeds the first,” calling it a first in the MCC partnership; said democracy must rest on three essential pillars, namely strong, credible institutions managed by people of quality, and freedom, which presupposes the security of persons, property and capital, with the last pillar, infrastructure, putting the energy question back at the heart of the stakes of prosperity.

a7078.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.name: Boni Yayi
a7078.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.speech: Indicated that the exclusive orientation of the American financing towards the energy sector comes at just the right moment to bring about a qualitative transformation of the Beninese economy: “The reforms will make it possible to support the regulatory authority, questions of tariff-setting, to open the sector to private actors, with legal documents allowing public-private partnership to be supported,” he insisted; confided that the expected investments should allow the installation of a generating capacity of about 78 MW, more than half of it devoted to renewable energy.

a7078.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.name: Boni Yayi
a7078.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a7078.speech: Reassured his interlocutor of the dispatch of 800 Beninese soldiers to reinforce the ranks of the multinational force being created to defeat the Islamic State in West Africa, and requested the logistical and financial support of the United States so that the mission assigned to this force may be crowned with success within a short time.

a7078.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.name: Joe Biden
a7078.title: Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.speech: Maintained: “The second compact is not automatic. This compact is a consequence of your personal leadership, which has made an enormous difference,” welcoming the fact that the USA is strengthening its partnership with a country that is exemplary in matters of democracy and freedoms; stressed: “Africa is a continent full of youthful energy and of promise. We must focus, create opportunities for that energy, and give young people promise.”

a7078.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.name: Joe Biden
a7078.title: Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.speech: Noted that the American programme helped to double the capacity of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, while acknowledging that many challenges remain to be met, including energy; said this second MCA compact is the largest MCC investment in the energy sector and the most important American support in the renewable-energy sub-sector; stated that MCA 2 will have an impact on the entire Beninese population in terms of access to electricity and will help to better manage public resources and promote private investment; concluded: “Obama's objective is to ensure energy for Africa, not only through the MCC but through all the vehicles that can be mobilised to bring light to every region of the continent. We are delighted to renew this partnership thanks to your commitment to democracy, good governance and the fight against corruption.”

a7078.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.name: Joe Biden
a7078.title: Vice-President of the United States of America
a7078.speech: Touched in his address on the restoration of security in the West African sub-region as his priority, in particular the merciless fight against the Islamist sect Boko Haram, and praised the leadership shown by Boni Yayi in mobilising the international community against the terrorist peril in the Sahelo-Saharan belt and his fight alongside the countries of the Lake Chad Basin Commission to end Boko Haram's atrocities.

a7252.speaker: Society for Water and Sanitation (NEWSAN)
a7252.name: Society for Water and Sanitation (NEWSAN)
a7252.speech: Explained the project's core objective is to improve WASH system services and foster community engagement to eliminate cholera risks and enhance public health, which involves improving access to clean water and sanitation facilities, supporting national cholera control plans, targeting cholera hotspots, strengthening community capacity, and enhancing monitoring and response systems ; the group said: "The project has now formally kicked off with effective advocacy by the NEWSAN LUWASH Team in Lagos to state officials and traditional leaders aimed at clarifying the project's scope, identifying challenges and mitigations, enhancing communication, and secure stakeholder buy-in, which will lay a strong foundation for successful project implementation by establishing a shared understanding of objectives, outcomes, roles, responsibilities, and timelines. Today, the NEWSAN LUWASH Team paid an advocacy visit and received the buy-in and support of the Executive Chairmen Ajeromi Ifelodun Local Government Area represented by the Deputy Chairman, Hon. Lucky Uduikhue along with Head of Department, Environmental Services and Waste Management, Mr. Idris L.O. at the LGA secretariat."

a7252.speaker: Hon. Lucky Uduikhue, Deputy Chairman, Ajeromi Ifelodun Local Government Area
a7252.name: Hon. Lucky Uduikhue
a7252.title: Deputy Chairman, Ajeromi Ifelodun Local Government Area
a7252.speech: Received the team and thanked them for the laudable project and assured the NEWSAN LUWASH team of his support and buy-in and is optimistic for a good delivery at the end of the project ; gave the go ahead to NEWSAN to commence implementation and asked the team to liaise with the Department of Environmental Services moving forward.

a7252.speaker: Evans Enwefah, programme officer, NEWSAN LUWASH
a7252.name: Evans Enwefah
a7252.title: programme officer, NEWSAN LUWASH
a7252.speech: Thanked the Deputy Chairman and the HOD Environmental Services and Waste Management for their support and assured them of effective delivery of the project in the LGA.

a7281.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a7281.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a7281.speech: According to UNHCR, more than 20 million people are forcibly displaced by weather related sudden onset hazards each year and 12 million of them are from Africa.

a7281.speaker: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a7281.name: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a7281.speech: According to the IPCC, agriculture accounts for about 75% of the labor force.

a7281.speaker: CNN
a7281.name: CNN
a7281.speech: As CNN indicated, on March 2017, more than 100 people died in Somalia in 48 hours.

a7281.speaker: UN assessment
a7281.name: UN assessment
a7281.speech: Estimates that 4.7 million people, nearly 40% of Somalia's population, are in need of humanitarian assistance.

a7390.speaker: Western countries
a7390.name: Western countries
a7390.speech: Condemned the coup, demanding the release of the detained ministers and threatening to cut off aid if the army did not share power with civilians.

a7390.speaker: The New York Times (report)
a7390.name: The New York Times (report)
a7390.speech: Reported that the Sudanese army carried out an air raid last Monday on the Darfur region, targeting a crowded market; the report contains videos and images taken after the attack in the town of Tura, a small locality in North Darfur, showing dozens of charred bodies and human remains scattered across a vast area in flames in the town's market, and adds that this massacre comes on top of other atrocities already reported in Darfur ; mentions several explosions, and concludes by underlining that the Sudanese army has repeatedly been accused of indiscriminate bombing of areas controlled by the RSF, often causing the deaths of dozens of civilians in a single attack, most of these attacks also having taken place in Darfur.

a7390.speaker: Satellite images and NASA fire-monitoring satellite data (cited in the report)
a7390.name: Satellite images and NASA fire-monitoring satellite data (cited in the report)
a7390.speech: Showed that an area of about 10,000 square metres had burned on Monday.

a7390.speaker: Avaaz, international human rights organisation
a7390.name: Avaaz
a7390.title: international human rights organisation
a7390.speech: Estimated, on the basis of local groups, that the death toll exceeded 200.

a7390.speaker: Eyewitness in a video filmed at the scene (anonymous)
a7390.name: Eyewitness in a video filmed at the scene (anonymous)
a7390.speech: States that four missiles struck the market, one hitting its centre and the three others hitting its surroundings.

a7390.speaker: Emergency Lawyers group, which documents violations during the war in Sudan
a7390.name: Emergency Lawyers group
a7390.title: which documents violations during the war in Sudan
a7390.speech: Accused the army of carrying out a deadly bombardment in northern Darfur, in one of the deadliest strikes since the start of the conflict two years ago, stating that the bombardment caused “the death of hundreds of civilians and dozens of seriously wounded.”

a7390.speaker: Two Sudanese who took part in the burial operations (anonymous)
a7390.name: Two Sudanese who took part in the burial operations (anonymous)
a7390.speech: Told AFP that they had counted “270 bodies buried and 380 wounded.”

a7390.speaker: United Nations
a7390.name: United Nations
a7390.speech: On Tuesday condemned the continuing attacks against civilians.

a7390.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN Secretary-General
a7390.name: Stephane Dujarric
a7390.title: spokesman for the UN Secretary-General
a7390.speech: “We are extremely concerned by the persistent attacks against civilians across the country. Last night, in Darfur, air strikes caused dozens of casualties at a market.”

a7390.speaker: African Union
a7390.name: African Union
a7390.speech: Described the October 2021 military coup as “a coup against a civilian government”; Sudan's membership remains “suspended” since then.

a7390.speaker: Maher Abu al-Joukh, leader of the Forces of Change movement
a7390.name: Maher Abu al-Joukh
a7390.title: leader of the Forces of Change movement
a7390.speech: States that “the authorities in Sudan are effectively isolated at the regional and international levels. This isolation is exacerbated by the reduction of conflicts between the regional powers, which has highlighted their lack of seriousness about ending the war.”

a7390.speaker: Mona Abdel Fattah, writer
a7390.name: Mona Abdel Fattah
a7390.title: writer
a7390.speech: Writes that the situation in Sudan was already no better before the war between the army and the RSF: “During the three decades of Omar al-Bashir's rule, the country sank into international isolation and experienced political and economic crises.” ; adds that “after the measures imposed by Burhan in 2021 and the cancellation of the Constitutional Declaration, the situation in Sudan became extremely complex. The country's future depended on the return of civilians to power, a condition set by the countries and organisations that were ready to help Sudan. But the war broke out in April 2023, leading to a freeze in external relations with many states and bodies.”

a7390.speaker: Human rights organisations and the international community
a7390.name: Human rights organisations and the international community
a7390.speech: Hailed Chad's measure granting Sudanese refugees the right to work as a model to be followed by other neighbouring countries hosting large numbers of Sudanese refugees.

a7390.speaker: Yasser Al-Atta, assistant to the chief of staff of the Sudanese armed forces
a7390.name: Yasser Al-Atta
a7390.title: assistant to the chief of staff of the Sudanese armed forces
a7390.speech: Declared that “the airports of N'Djamena and Amdjarass are legitimate targets” for his army.

a7390.speaker: Chad (government reaction)
a7390.name: Chad (government reaction)
a7390.speech: Reacted with astonishment to these statements, saying they “may be interpreted as a declaration of war if they are followed by action,” and warning that it “reserves the right to retaliate” in the event of an attack on its territory.

a7390.speaker: Kenya
a7390.name: Kenya
a7390.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment to restoring political and security stability in Sudan in coordination with the UN and the African Union, stressing that “the conflict in Sudan continues to destroy a country which, only four years ago, was on the path to stability, democracy and prosperity for its people.”

a7472.speaker: El Pais Mexico (newspaper)
a7472.name: El Pais Mexico (newspaper)
a7472.speech: Had pompously headlined: “The hour of women has come.”

a7472.speaker: Claudia Sheinbaum, President of Mexico
a7472.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
a7472.title: President of Mexico
a7472.speech: Launched her electoral campaign on 1 March 2024 with the slogan “LONG LIVE ANDRES MANUEL LOPEZ OBRADOR!” ; “We shall have, together, to preserve the legacy of this man who is today in the National Palace and who has changed the history of our country for the better.”

a7472.speaker: Insight Crime
a7472.name: Insight Crime
a7472.speech: Reports that the country recorded 23.3 homicides per 100,000 inhabitants in 2023, that is 30,500 fatal victims, a rate that places Mexico in 14th place worldwide.

a7472.speaker: Claudia Sheinbaum, President of Mexico
a7472.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
a7472.title: President of Mexico
a7472.speech: Announced, as soon as she was sworn in on 1 October, an ambitious plan to strengthen security in the most violent zones of the country, with large-scale security actions among her priorities for the first hundred days directed at regions most affected by organised crime, a strategy targeting the ten municipalities with the highest homicide rates, and insisted on the importance of the intelligence tool for dismantling the cartels.

a7472.speaker: Women in the Workplace 2024 annual study, by McKinsey & Company and LeanIn.org
a7472.name: Women in the Workplace 2024 annual study
a7472.title: by McKinsey & Company and LeanIn.org
a7472.speech: According to the study, women possess qualities that considerably favour the success of private-sector companies and public institutions; they generally approach leadership with more empathy, inclusion and willingness to build connections.

a7472.speaker: Jack Zenger and Joseph Folkman (analysis presented in 2019)
a7472.name: Jack Zenger and Joseph Folkman (analysis presented in 2019)
a7472.speech: Indicates that women excel in several key managerial domains and outperform men in 17 out of 19 categories, being notably more competent in taking initiative, in resilience and in personal development; women managers are generally better in terms of results, integrity, developing others and inspiring teams.

a7484.speaker: Vanguard Student Unification Party (SUP), University of Liberia
a7484.name: Vanguard Student Unification Party (SUP)
a7484.title: University of Liberia
a7484.speech: Has strongly condemned the administration’s decision to classify the ongoing vacation school as a full academic semester, describing the move as an “affront” to the student body.

a7484.speaker: Sylvester Wheeler, SUP Chairman
a7484.name: Sylvester Wheeler
a7484.title: SUP Chairman
a7484.speech: Expressed deep disappointment in the University’s President, Dr. Layli Maparyan, citing her failure to address pressing issues affecting students and staff; warned that SUP can no longer guarantee a “peaceful space” on campus if their demands are not swiftly met ; “We reject the administration’s decision to label vacation school as a second semester. Vacation school is intended to allow students to take a limited number of courses, up to three for undergraduates and two for graduate and professional students. It should never serve as a substitute for a full semester.”

a7484.speaker: Sylvester Wheeler, SUP Chairman
a7484.name: Sylvester Wheeler
a7484.title: SUP Chairman
a7484.speech: Called for a quick resolution to ongoing problems with the university’s add-and-drop process, which has left many students uncertain about their academic standing and at risk of missing grades.

a7484.speaker: Sylvester Wheeler, SUP Chairman
a7484.name: Sylvester Wheeler
a7484.title: SUP Chairman
a7484.speech: Demanded the public release of an investigative report related to the suspension and dismissal of several UL staff members, including the Vice President for Fiscal Affairs; argued that the continued withholding of the report undermines transparency and contradicts President Maparyan’s stated commitment to integrity.

a7484.speaker: Sylvester Wheeler, SUP Chairman
a7484.name: Sylvester Wheeler
a7484.title: SUP Chairman
a7484.speech: Criticized the recent hiring of over 15 new staff members, some allegedly connected to USAID, while existing underpaid employees continue to be neglected, labelling the hiring practices as “questionable” and lacking merit-based transparency.

a7484.speaker: Sylvester Wheeler, SUP Chairman
a7484.name: Sylvester Wheeler
a7484.title: SUP Chairman
a7484.speech: Condemned the deteriorating condition of the university’s infrastructure, pointing to a shortage of buses, inadequate seating, unsanitary restrooms, and dilapidated buildings as evidence of administrative negligence.

a7484.speaker: Odecious Mulbah, SUP Secretary-General
a7484.name: Odecious Mulbah
a7484.title: SUP Secretary-General
a7484.speech: Called on President Maparyan to act decisively. “If these issues are not addressed immediately, the administration should expect more robust actions from the student body.”
